Sports.title: Arsenal show mark of champions but Nottingham Forest borefest gives Arteta plenty to ponder
Sports.content:
Arsenal show mark of champions but Nottingham Forest borefest gives Arteta plenty to ponder

NOTTINGHAM FOREST 0-1 ARSENAL: Noni Madueke's deflected strike 10 minutes from time closed the gap at the top of the Premier League to just three points

View 3 Images Madueke celebrates his winer for Arsenal (Image: Godfrey Pitt/Action Plus/Shutterstock)

The army of away fans did not really care by the end.

‌



‌



Noni Madueke’s deflected winner got the job done at the City Ground and earned Arsenal a precious victory and three points as they closed the gap on Manchester City at the top.

‌



Incredibly, Arsenal’s previous two trips to Nottingham Forest had ended as goalless draws and actually it was probably the worst of the three games in the boredom trilogy.

‌



Arsenal did not manage a shot on target until the 80th minute when Madueke’s shot flew into the net to delight the travelling fans behind that goal.

Forest have also now gone eight hours and 26 minutes without a home goal in all competitions. Yes, it was that bad. And more. It has not been an ideal start for new Forest boss Oliver Glasner with just one win from their opening seven games.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Ultimately, it is just about getting the win, closing down the gap at the top and, for Mikel Arteta, he will be happy just to get the three points.

You could call it the mark of champions by winning when they do not play well and also getting a victory at a tough away ground which the City Ground undoubtedly still is.

‌



It was also a big moment for Madueke who has been so hit and miss since his £52m arrival from Chelsea in the summer of 2025. Madueke has never been able to hold down a regular starting place and often looks like a fish out of water on the left wing.

But, in fairness, Madueke did liven things up after coming on for the ineffective Eberechi Eze at half time and scored after cutting in from the left wing.

However, the wider problem for Arsenal is they actually look worse up front than last season and yet they were supposed to improve their squad in the summer.

‌



Instead, they sold Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Martinelli, brought in Christos Tzolis - who is currently out injured - and look so short of ideas in attack.

View 3 Images Madueke repaid Arteta's faith (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

How can you possibly win the title - and then make the strike force worse? They missed out on Morgan Rogers and got horribly played by Vinicius Junior.

‌



They now have fewer options and yet are trying desperately to defend their title and, on this evidence, it is going to be a long hard slog.

Arteta said on Friday that he regards Kai Havertz as a 25-goal striker but he headed their best first-half chance over the bar.

Bukayo Saka was up against Neco Williams down his flank and, despite the Forest full-back getting booked after just 17 minutes, failed to really test him enough.

‌



Arsenal looked short of ideas and inspiration. The first half was shocking. So much for Super Sunday. Sky should rebrand it Switch Off Sunday and ask both clubs to give their TV cash back. It was that bad.

Arteta rolled the dice with his substitutes and was lucky that Forest were so toothless up front themselves even though Liam Delap worked and ran himself into the ground.

View 3 Images Liam Delap was Forest's biggest threat (Image: Getty Images)

‌



The substitutes made a difference for Arsenal. Arsenal produced by far and away their best move of the match in the 72nd minute as Saka and Martin Odegaard combined before Jurrien Timber’s cut back set up Declan Rice only for the England midfielder to smash the ball over the bar.

But Arsenal were finally knocking on the door. Forest substitute Ibrahim Sangare failed to clear properly, Rice fed Madueke who cut into the box and the Arsenal winger’s shot deflected in off Jair Cunha.

That was a stroke of luck. There were hearts in mouths when Forest defender Murillo raced into the box, had a sight of goal in the dying stages but blazed over. It was a let-off but was a reflection of the game.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta masterstroke sees Arsenal earn gritty win against Nottingham Forest
Sports.content:
Arsenal ensured they kept pace with Manchester City in the early Premier League title race after squeezing past by Nottingham Forest.

The Gunners struggled to break down their hosts throughout the majority of the game, albeit Declan Rice was guilty of passing up a golden opportunity.

Their opener eventually came late on through Noni Madueke, whose deflected effort was enough to seal victory for the champions.

The win leaves Mikel Arteta's side sitting second and three points behind City. Forest in the meantime remain in the drop zone despite their resolute performance going unrewarded.

‌

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Madueke makes an impact

Following a less-than inspiring first-half in the East-Midlands, Arsenal boss Arteta opted for a change at the break, with Eberechi Eze being replaced by Noni Madeueke. While substitutions have proven so fruitful for the Arsenal boss over recent seasons, it looked as though the opposite might be true at the City Ground.

Madueke endured a nightmare start to his outing after picking up a booking. He also had very little impact from an attacking standpoint.

‌



That was until the final ten minutes of the game. Madueke picked up the ball on the left flank, cut inside and let fly, with his effort flying past Mats Sels via a deflection.

It was a bold move from Arteta, but one that was absolutely the correct one.

Delap Forest's biggest outlet

After scoring his first Forest in the win against Villa last month, striker Liam Delap was once again his side's biggest threat against Arsenal. And while he didn't quite manage to get on the scoresheet, it was still an impressive performance from the forward.

His tireless running gave Forest a real focal point, while Delap's strength and physicality allowed Forest to move up the pitch once he had successfully managed to hold the ball up.

‌



Of course, goals need to come more regularly for Delap now, having scored just two Premier League goals over the past 18 months. But more performances like this are really encouraging.

View 2 Images Liam Delap was Forest's biggest threat (Image: Getty Images)

Arsenal's City Ground hoodoo comes to an end

Arteta's side have not had the best of luck at the City Ground over the past few years. They had only won on one of their last five visits to Forest - a record that includes a rotten FA Cup defeat, as well as consecutive 0-0 draws.

In fact, their only win at the City Ground since Forest's promotion back to the top fight came back in January 2024.

‌



So it was no surprise to see Arsenal struggle for fluency. They failed to produce a single shot on target throughout the first 75 minutes and never really looked like taking the lead.

That was until, of course, Madueke converted. And it was just about enough to see Arsenal seal a hard-fought three points. It's an old cliche but champions find a way to win and that's exactly what they did.

Sports.title: Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner
Sports.content:
Leeds miss golden chance to pile misery on Man Utd - but match didn't deserve a winner

LEEDS 1-1 MANCHESTER UNITED: Bryan Mbeumo fired the Red Devils ahead before the break but Dominic Calvert-Lewin struck in the second half to earn a point for the hosts

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin scores the equaliser for Leeds (Image: ADAM VAUGHAN/EPA/Shutterstock)

Dominic Calvert-Lewin denied Manchester United their first win in six games - to pile more pressure on Michael Carrick.

‌



‌



Calvert-Lewin's second half equaliser cancelled out Bryan Mbeumo's 35th minute strike, to make it honours even at a white hot Elland Road.

‌



But if Carrick returned across the Pennines feeling satisfied, he shouldn't have done. The United boss insists he has the best job possible and is still 'loving it'.

‌



But no manager in their right mind should be loving the fact their side has not won a single game for more than five weeks.

Or kept a clean sheet in the league all season. At this rate, United will be airing the club's dirty laundry in public again, by sacking another manager.

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Carrick had needed this trip to Elland Road like a hole in the head. The cauldron of hate is bad enough in normal circumstances, let alone when United had not won in five games in all competitions.

Leeds never need an excuse to pile pain on their bitter rivals, but on this occasion the hosts must have been relishing the visit of Carrick's men more than ever.

‌



Leeds went into this clash above United in the table. The last time this happened was back in 2002, which was also the last time Leeds beat United at home. But this time round United appeared vulnerable and there for the taking.

Not least because United started with a right back at left back, and a centre back at right back. While Lisandro Martinez owed his manager a big performance, considering his outburst in the wake of the defeat at Atletico Madrid.

Most of the first half was high on toxicity and low on quality. Ethan Ampadu made three crunching tackles on Andrey Santos, Kobbie Mainoo and Mbeumo.

‌



View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo opened the scoring (Image: Stu Forster/Getty Images)

While Bruno Fernandes and Gabriel Gudmundsson were booked for two crude challenges of their own. This was no place for shrinking violets. But a football match broke out just before the half hour mark.

Nico Elvedi saw a header well saved by Senne Lammens. While at the opposite end Youri Tielemans put a chance on a plate for Mbeumo, who made a complete meal of it by heading wide with just James Trafford to beat.

‌



Trafford then had to charge from goal to stop Amad Diallo. It was fast, furious and frantic in equal measure. But 10 minutes before the break Mbeumo made amends to give United the lead.

He brushed aside a feeble challenge from James Justin to meet another Tielemans cross and beat Trafford with a cool finish. Ao Tanaka shot straight at Lammens before Calvert-Lewin headed just wide, as Leeds looked to hit back.

View 3 Images Dominic Calvert-Lewin equalised for Leeds (Image: Anna Gowthorpe/Shutterstock)

‌



Which they eventually did six minutes into the second half, when Calvert-Lewin lashed home from close range after United had failed to deal with a corner.

Leeds had their tails up, and Tanaka smashed a volley over the top. Harry Maguire was fortunate to avoid conceding a penalty after pulling Ampadu to the ground inside the box.

Tensions continued to simmer, with Ampadu and Fernandes involved in a spiteful exchange of words, while Tanaka left Diallo writhing in pain following a brutal - but legal - tackle.

Article continues below

Fernandes dragged a shot wide and Anton Stach blazed over as both sides went in search of winner. But in truth, the game didn't deserve one.

Sports.title: Neville delivers Carrick warning after Man Utd 'stepping stone' performance
Sports.content:
Sky Sports pundit Gary Neville believes Manchester United's 1-1 draw at Leeds could be a "stepping stone" but has warned that Michael Carrick will have a problem if his side are still 13th in the Premier League come January.

United have just seven points from seven league matches, winning just one of those, which is their fewest number of victories at this stage of a top-flight season for 40 years.

Despite extending their winless run in all competitions to six games with the draw at Elland Road, the performance was much improved, with Carrick's tactical tweaks making his side more compact and defensively solid.

Neville agreed with the United head coach's assessment that Sunday's performance at Elland Road was a step in the right direction.

Speaking on the Gary Neville podcast, the Sky Sports pundit said: "[There's] a depressed standard and a low expectation right now.

"But it'll feel like a stepping stone for Michael Carrick, and it'll feel like the first step on the ladder in the Premier League.

"They may take some confidence from that, and there might be a blueprint there. Maybe we have to bring Matheus Cunha, Marcus Rashford and others off the bench, and we might just have to have a go at being more solid."

'Carrick's got a problem if Man Utd 13th in January'

Image: Man Utd have just one win from seven Premier League matches

United's paltry points return has them sitting 13th in the Premier League after seven games, already five points adrift of fifth place, which was enough for Champions League qualification last season.

Neville says there is no need for panic just yet but feels United have to show signs of improvement over the next few weeks otherwise Carrick could find himself in hot water come the new year.

"I would say fourth would be a birdie, fifth would be par, and sixth would be a bogey," said Neville of his former club's targets for the season. "But they can't finish outside the top five, because then you're missing out on Champions League and it becomes a vicious circle.

"Then you can't get those players because they want to play in the Champions League and you can't get the money from it and you've lost the £60m-£70m and you're in the Europa League on Thursday nights.

"Fifth is a must for Michael Carrick to continue to grow and Manchester United continue to grow with investment.

"If they're 13th in January, he's got a problem because then you are what you are. Whereas I think it's still early enough, seven points from seven games, to say, 'okay, still early in the season'. You can't say that after 15 games.

"It has to change in the next few weeks: Bournemouth is really important and Chelsea away. And how he manages the games in between that.

"You've got to say fifth. You know that anything less than fifth is going to be a disappointment and a dropping standard from the start of the season where everybody expected them to finish.

"And at the moment, they're well short of that because you look at Brighton, Liverpool, Aston Villa - they look like they're picking up a little bit. It's difficult."

'Baleba staying fit is going to be critical'

Image: Carlos Baleba made his Man Utd debut against Tottenham

Neville has seen encouraging signs from Carlos Baleba's start to life as a Manchester United player and feels the midfielder staying fit is crucial for Carrick this season.

Signed from Brighton for £70m at the end of the summer window, the 21-year-old arrived with an ankle injury that has kept him from featuring until he came on in the second half of last Saturday's 1-1 draw against 10-man Tottenham.

Baleba has started the last two games, at Atletico Madrid and Leeds, and brought an added steel to United's midfield alongside fellow summer-signing Andrey Santos.

"I know he had a difficult season last year at Brighton, but you watch him in his first couple of games or so for United, and he's got something," said Neville. "He's got a bit of strength about him, he's got a presence.

"Him staying fit is gonna be absolutely critical, I can understand why Michael Carrick took him off with 20 minutes to go [at Leeds], because he's played [nearly] three games in a week.

"Maybe he doesn't play him against Como on Wednesday. We're not throwing the Champions League away, but Manchester United have to beat Bournemouth next weekend.

"I just wonder whether that Santos-Baleba partnership is going to stay there for a bit, and let a couple of [the attacking players] float around in front, and be a lot more solid, make sure we're not giving as much space away.

"I'm sick of Manchester United's team being easy to play against, and Michael Carrick will be sick of it."

Sports.title: Arsenal win with one shot on target as Forest sink into bottom three
Sports.content:
Arsenal's only shot on target proved enough to snatch victory at Nottingham Forest through Noni Madueke's deflected strike, keeping the champions within touching distance of Premier League leaders Manchester City and condemning Forest to the relegation zone.

After 80 frustrating minutes at the City Ground, substitute Madueke cut inside from the left and fired towards goal. His strike deflected off Jair Cunha, wrong-footed Matz Sels and found the net to settle a game in which Arsenal had struggled to turn possession into chances.

Arsenal had dominated the ball but registered no shots on target in the first half. Kai Havertz headed wide from a Declan Rice free-kick while Gabriel's set-piece effort was cleared almost off the line by Ousmane Diomande.

Forest made life difficult for Mikel Arteta's side, defending resolutely and threatening on the counter. Murillo almost salvaged a point in stoppage time with a superb solo run, driving at the Arsenal defence before curling narrowly wide. Ezri Konsa then made a crucial late challenge to deny Liam Delap.

However, despite their opportunities, it was the same old story for Oliver Glasner's side, who failed to find a breakthrough.

The result takes Arsenal to 18 points, three behind leaders Manchester City. For Forest, the frustration deepens. They drop into the relegation zone and are still waiting for their first home league goal of the season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Noni Madueke's deflected strike gives Arsenal the lead

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Murillo goes close against Arsenal

Analysis: Eze must prove his worth as Arsenal's main man after Madueke shines

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

Eberechi Eze has spent a year at Arsenal since leaving Crystal Palace, but questions remain over whether he is ready to become one of the club's leading figures as their ambitions continue to grow.

His talent is undeniable. The real concern is whether he can influence games consistently, and the trip to Nottingham Forest presented another opportunity to silence his doubters.

With Arsenal struggling to break down Forest, Eze had the chance to make a difference. Instead, he was substituted at half-time, watching from the sidelines as Noni Madueke replaced him and went on to score the 80th-minute winner.

Roy Keane's assessment on Sky Sports was telling, suggesting his concerns extended beyond a single performance.

"We're still waiting for him, the talent is there," Keane said. "We just want him to be at Arsenal and be able to take responsibility and try to be the main man at a big club."

That is the challenge facing Eze. At Crystal Palace, he was the focal point, the player expected to create chances and turn games in his team's favour. At Arsenal, however, talent alone will not earn him that status. He must deliver consistently, particularly in tight contests when his team need inspiration.

Ian Wright offered some important context, describing Eze as a "moments player" who benefits from having players around him and can become isolated on the left.

There is merit to that argument. Eze offers a different threat to Madueke, whose pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders gave Arsenal a fresh dimension in the second half.

Yet that only underlines the challenge facing the former Palace man. While Madueke seized his opportunity and made an immediate impact, Eze failed to leave his mark on the contest.

Competition for places is healthy at a club with Arsenal's ambitions. For Eze, though, the task is no longer simply to showcase his ability in flashes. He must demonstrate that he can influence games regularly, take responsibility when his team need him and establish himself as a first-choice player.

The talent is there. Now, Eze must prove he can turn that potential into consistent performances and become one of Arsenal's main men.

Forest's lack of goals has caught up with them

Analysis by Sky Sports' William Bitibiri:

There was only so long Nottingham Forest could rely on defensive resilience before their lack of goals caught up with them. Now they are in the relegation zone.

Oliver Glasner's side have failed to score in every Premier League home game this season, and their defeat to Arsenal highlighted why they are in trouble.

Forest competed and created opportunities, but lacked the quality in the final third to make their efforts count.

Liam Delap struggled to make an impact against Arsenal's defence, summing up a frustrating afternoon. Forest needed someone to take responsibility, but their attacking play lacked conviction.

That is the worry for Glasner. Defensive organisation can only take a team so far; they still need goals to win matches.

Forest are now in the relegation zone with just five points. Their performances offer some encouragement, but until they find a reliable source of goals at the City Ground, it is difficult to see their situation improving.

19: Forest threaten - Riccardo Calafiori's mistake gives Forest an opening, but Dan Ndoye shoots into the side netting.

26: Arsenal nearly break through - Gabriel's effort deflects off Saliba and is cleared close to the line by Diomande.

37: Havertz misses - The German heads wide from Rice's free-kick.

46: Madueke replaces Eze - Arteta makes a half-time change.

54: Delap goes close - His effort takes a deflection and goes wide.

66: Arsenal make three changes - Jurrien Timber, Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino come on.

80: GOAL! Forest 0-1 Arsenal - Madueke's strike deflects off Cunha and beats Sels.

89: Forest waste a chance - Callum Hudson-Odoi sets up Chris Wood, but Declan Rice blocks his shot.

90+2: Murillo nearly equalises - The defender drives forward and curls narrowly wide.

90+3: Konsa saves Arsenal - The defender times a vital challenge to deny Delap.

Arteta: We knew margins would be small

Mikel Arteta to Sky Sports:

"We did something we didn't do in the two seasons before and that is win the game.

"We knew the margins would be small unless you open up the game much earlier, which we had two chances to do.

"The longer the game goes on, they have more belief and that's when you have to take more risks and that when the game can break.

"But we talked about it. We had to be so patient, without getting frustrated.

"It was tough to generate open chances against them. And we have to take them when we get them.

"We had another three chances [in the gme] that should have been on target.

"And not only on target, but they should have been goal.

"That's the difference, you have to be clinical."

Glasner: Have to take your chances against the champions

Oliver Glasner to Sky Sports:

"I think everybody feels the result is unfair today (in terms of the way we performed).

"But it's another defeat and another game when we couldn't score at the City Ground.

"But the performance today, especially defensively was of the top level.

"It was their only shot on target (that Arsenal scored from) and this one was deflected and Arsenal took the win.

"We also had our moments and it's important when you play the champions you take your moments.

"But today, the performance, effort, spirit and energy we had was on a very good level. But the result is frustrating."

Sports.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
Sports.content:
At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun.

Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble.

How do you solve what is, on revenue versus results, the worst-run club in world football? By changing the name of the latest patsy on the touchline, of course. For now a hard-fought point is perhaps enough to stave off that pre-programmed emergency response.

Stand down the cowboy cops. Call off the blue and white saloons. Although with a run of Bournemouth, Chelsea, Aston Villa and Liverpool next up in the league it will no doubt soon be time to go out there and arrest Lee Harvey Oswald again. What’s that you say? OK, well, dig him up again. Re-arrest him. Whatever it takes. Someone has to stop these lone gunmen, these managerial magic bullet merchants from derailing the Manchester United supremacy.

This was a dual-track football match between Leeds and Manchester United, on the face of it a good, even game between two teams of well-matched players. A 1-1 draw was fair in the end, although Leeds played well and probably should have won. But of course they won’t be the story.

Instead this game had already been billed as that familiar thing, a referendum on the future of Michael Carrick. A stay of execution for a week or two. Or another livestreamed firing squad for the Super Sunday cameras.

There has been a predictable sense of low comedy about Carrick’s own transformation in the United dugout this season. It was always going to be the case that his widely praised qualities in victory, blazer, T-shirt, jawline, inscrutable sense of calm, would become his fatal flaws in defeat.

Where’s the passion, the whirling arms, the range of tailored collars? At Elland Road Carrick simply looked drained in the second half as United were pegged back and overrun at times, the beard a little more ragged, the hair unkempt but still sweeping, the look of a brave, doomed tugboat captain resigned now to the approaching tsunami wave on the horizon.

A point leaves United 13th in the league and still struggling to reverse a dreadful start to the season. But it was a good game for two people. First for Carrick, who remains a million miles away from creating the problems afflicting this club, even if you accept that his presence as head coach is one of them.

Michael Carrick did not hire Michael Carrick. Getting rid of Michael Carrick is, by definition, not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. But it might just help to prolong them. Whatever his ultimate ceiling, it is surely worth keeping him just to try, for once, to do something different.

View image in fullscreen The Manchester United director of football, Jason Wilcox (centre), and chief executive officer Omar Berrada (right) watch on at Elland Road. Photograph: Annabel Lee-Ellis/PA

This was also a good game for Lisandro Martínez, who went off injured at half-time with United 1-0 up, and who was also vindicated in his allegedly controversial (translation: entirely correct) comments on the club hierarchy in midweek.

United’s energetic first-half performance clarified one half of this. The players are committed in support of the manager, at least to the best of their ability. The second half made the other half of the argument, that this remains a mismatched, lopsided, cut-and-paste squad, always likely to be pulled apart by opponents as urgent as this Leeds team, which fully deserves its current seventh place in the table.

The problems are so obvious it is barely worth repeating them. But here goes. The third-richest club in the world played a second half with three of its back four out of position. Harry Maguire, signed under Ole Gunnar Solskjær, remains the best straight defender. But Maguire is also essentially a man-shaped solid wood armoire in a pair of shorts at this stage in his career, always the slowest person on any pitch, which means you will not be able to cover space, play a high line or counterattack without leaving yourself exposed to the counter-counter.

So good luck, guys. And remember Omar, who gave you this whisky bottle and loaded pistol of a squad, will be watching.

This was made painfully clear after half-time as Martínez went off and Noussair Mazraoui came on. Leeds scored an equaliser that felt structurally inevitable. They found space down their right side repeatedly. At times they seemed to be constantly peppering the seats behind the United goal, like a group of kids hammering a ball against a garage door. By the end Leeds had more possession, more shots on target and just looked a happier, better structured entity than the travelling heritage exhibit at the other end.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The key point here is to accept that all of this is entirely logical. This is not a mystery, a haunted house, a place of bad voodoo. Why do we talk about Manchester United so much? For obvious reasons. It’s a massive part of the English football landscape. Mainly, though, because this is a story of mind-bending waste, real-time elite-level incompetence played out on a weekly basis.

Yes, you could sack Michael Carrick. It won’t change much. Let’s destroy Eddie Howe for a bit instead. But the available evidence suggests every single person making executive decisions here is outmatched and outmanoeuvred.

There is a reason Manchester United feels like one of those high street legacy chain shops just before it collapses, piles of Quality Street by the door, a rat in the lingerie department, destined to become a pop-up vape shop run by Albanian money launderers. There’s a reason it feels so badly run. This is because: it is.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez, who criticised the Manchester United hierarchy in midweek, went off injured at half-time against Leeds. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

We know the Glazer ownership has zero interest in minding the details, that this has been a wonderful acquisition whatever the performance on the pitch, an asset supremely sweated. We know also that Sir Jim Ratcliffe is pub-level incoherent on the details he promised to fix. Remember when he was going to sit down and decide what the “style of football” would be? How’s that working out?

Instead Carrick is left shuffling a first XI acquired by endlessly revolving administrations. Here United had four defenders signed under Erik ten Hag, two Ruben Amorim recruits, two from the mist-shrouded age of Solskjær. No players were recruited under Ralf Rangnick, of course. But then Rangnick wanted to sign Erling Haaland, Luis Díaz, and Julian Álvarez, which all sounds far too sensible.

An organisation can be built with many hands. But not when so many of those hands appear to be so far from best in class it’s hard to work out which class they’re supposed to be attending. John Murtough, the former Manchester United football director, is currently director of global development at Atalanta, who have a 24,000-seat stadium and almost zero global presence. Meanwhile Berrada, the axeman, seems entirely invulnerable from the axe himself, despite the fact his job seems to orbit around resolving the consequences of his own mistakes.

United probably will sack their current manager before the year is out. This is the way this machine has to operate, always looking to buy itself, and those in the executive seats, a little more time on the payroll, an entity that has been hollowed out and allowed to rust, run on buzzwords and brown paper and string. Meanwhile, over to you Michael. We’ll see you next week, and maybe even the week after that, for more of exactly the same.

Sports.title: Madueke breaks Nottingham Forest’s resistance as dogged Arsenal edge to victory
Sports.content:
The theme before kick-off was blanks. Or, more precisely, whether either team could stop firing them at the City Ground. It was a detail to make Oliver Glasner extremely uncomfortable that his Nottingham Forest team had still to score at their own stadium this season. Arsenal, meanwhile, had drawn 0-0 on their previous two visits to this part of the east Midlands. They had only one win in five here.

Forest’s frustrations under their new manager go on. It was another spirited performance from them, bits to like, especially a full-throttle performance from Liam Delap in the No 9 position. But, for the fifth time under Glasner, there was not a goal to celebrate in front of the home support.

It was a game that came to feel increasingly set up for the famous terrace chant. One-nil to the Ars-en-nal. Or, as the travelling hordes would have it, one-nil to the champions. Arsenal did not play well. They created little, finishing with just one shot on target. How Noni Madueke made it count.

On as a half-time substitute, the winger took a pass from Declan Rice in the 80th minute and had only one thing on his mind. To cut inside from the left and unload. The connection was pure and that was when he caught a break, which he has worked to earn after a difficult start to the season. The ball deflected off Jair Cunha and flew past the Forest goalkeeper, Matz Sels.

View image in fullscreen Liam Delap holds off Ezri Konsa at the City Ground. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Forest refused to accept the inevitable. Chris Wood, on as a substitute, delayed too long and saw Rice block. Murillo, of all players, danced inside from the left and curled off target. Delap was denied at the death by a thunderous Ezri Konsa block tackle. But it did feel inevitable. Forest, who missed the injured Morgan Gibbs-White, might have played all night and not scored. Arsenal had not forgotten their previous away fixture – the 3-0 defeat at Brighton. It remains the only blot on their season.

Arsenal had kicked off six points behind Manchester City, who have been perfect on the field in the league this season. Will it matter when the sanctions for their rule breaches are meted out? All Arsenal can do is play the situation as it stands and this was an occasion when the result was everything.

Mikel Arteta’s team dominated the ball. As they were always likely to do. They were determined to be patient. And yet they were flat and predictable until the closing stages. The lack of incisive movement was glaring. That said, Forest were compact out of possession in a 5-4-1 formation and hard to break down. They were resolved not to give up any easy yards.

Arsenal played their patterns. They tried to suck the life out of the home crowd, working on the principle that it is difficult for fans to get animated if their team do not have the ball. The first half drifted by in a lazy Sunday afternoon haze, no shots on target for either side.

Delap carried the physical fight; the Forest centre-forward was a willing and direct runner and he won a free-kick off Rice just outside the Arsenal box on 44 minutes. Neco Williams thumped it at Bruno Guimarães, who went down and stayed down. The Forest support were unhappy at what they perceived as Arsenal’s use of the dark arts. “Are you City in disguise?” they chanted.

View image in fullscreen Noni Madueke fires home – via a deflection – the only goal of the game. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Could a set piece provide the breakthrough? It felt the likeliest route. Murillo headed wide from a Forest corner in the 20th minute and was bloodied into the bargain; there was a whistle for a foul in the mass of bodies inside the six-yard box. At the other end, Kai Havertz headed over from a Rice free-kick on 37 minutes. He had a good look at the ball and was well-placed. It was a decent chance.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Arsenal have been a little barren in the first half this season. This was the seventh time in 10 matches since the Community Shield that they had failed to score in one. It has not been a problem. They needed to raise their levels for the second half.

Arteta’s first change was Madueke for Eberechi Eze on the left wing; an admission that the latter had failed to exert an influence. There was also a triple substitution on 66 minutes, the manager sending on Jurriën Timber, Mikel Merino and Viktor Gyökeres for Ben White, Guimarães and Havertz. He needed to shake things up because nothing was happening for his team. It was Forest who pushed after the restart, with Delap continuing to put himself about. He asked questions of Gabriel Magalhães, albeit the Arsenal defender tended to have the answers.

The minutes ticked down, the contest narrowing to a fine point and we waited to see whether there could be a moment, one big chance. Martin Ødegaard almost provided it in the 72nd minute when he released Timber with a lovely pass up the inside right. When he pulled back, Rice lifted wastefully high.

Glasner’s decision to introduce Ibrahim Sangaré for Dan Ndoye shortly afterwards was telling. Sangaré’s mission was to bolster the Forest midfield and yet he was slow to react to a half-cleared ball. When Rice played the pass, Madueke took over.

“We showed a champion spirit,” Madueke said. “Maybe last season, this game might not have gone for us. We have the extra belief and mentality.”

Sports.title: Gómez halfway-line wondergoal sparks Brighton’s 5-0 thrashing of sorry Crystal Palace
Sports.content:
At last, Fabian Hürzeler has the scalp that matters most to all Brighton fans and in humiliating fashion. Diego Gómez’s breathtaking goal-of-the-season contender from the halfway line, à la David Beckham, was the highlight of another hugely impressive performance from the Premier League’s top scorers as they continued their flying start to the season.

Not since a 4-1 thrashing here in February 2024 under Roberto De Zerbi had Brighton tasted victory against their arch rivals from up the A23 – a run of four matches. But having been handed the initiative by Jaydee Canvot’s own goal, a stunned Palace found themselves 3-0 down after 10 minutes. It got even worse for Pierre Sage after Brighton extended their lead through Gómez’s wonderstrike and Yasin Ayari, with Charalampos Kostoulas adding a fourth after half-time and the substitute Jack Hinshelwood’s late strike matching their record 5-0 win over Palace from 1956 in Division Three South.

The concerning news for Sage, whose decision to field the teenager Honest Ahanor and 20-year-old Canvot in defence backfired spectacularly, is that two of his predecessors – Patrick Vieira and Roy Hodgson – were relieved of their jobs not long after losing against Brighton. Palace have conceded more goals than any other Premier League side this season and it is understood that there have been some disagreements behind the scenes since the Frenchman took over from Oliver Glasner in the summer, although it remains to be seen whether the chair, Steve Parish, will act on suggestions from the gleeful Brighton supporters during the second half that he will be sacked in the morning.

“It’s not my decision. I don’t know,” said Sage when asked if he will be given time to fix Palace’s leaky defence. “I will always give my best. I just want to apologise to the fans because it’s not normal to show this face. My feeling after the game is shame.”

It was Hürzleler who was on the receiving end of that chant in February after Palace’s smash-and-grab victory on the south coast. How things have changed. His vibrant side now find themselves in the conversation for Champions League qualification and they have a squad that also looks capable of coping with the demands of European football.

View image in fullscreen Yasin Ayari’s deflected effort results in Brighton’s third goal. Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/Reuters

“The last game against Palace made me really grounded, having this criticism. It wasn’t easy,” said Hürzeler. “Now we sit here in a completely different mood, with a feeling of being really proud to beat Palace. I experienced some derbies and I’m part of this club, I’m part of the journey, that’s why I’m also part of the history. The players deserve it for the hard work they did in the last month because they really stuck together, they faced adversity. They were always there for each other.”

The usual hostility greeted the travelling fans after Sussex police had warned they would be deploying extra officers to deal with what remains very much a grudge match. But a torrential downpour before kick-off didn’t dampen Brighton’s desire for revenge. They tore into Palace’s inexperienced defence from the first whistle and Canvot was caught flat-footed as he headed a pinpoint free-kick from Pascal Gross past Walter Benítez.

The Palace goalkeeper could then only watch in horror when Olivier Boscagli fed Gómez on the halfway line after Adam Wharton had lost possession cheaply and the ball sailed over his head into the net after the sweetest of contacts. No wonder that Hürzeler has been urging his players to take more shots from long range this season – they were already the division’s top scorers with efforts from outside the box this season with four. Gómez’s strike from 51 metres was the Premier League goal from furthest out since Wayne Rooney scored from 58 metres for Everton against West Ham in November 2017.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Things got even better for Brighton when a flowing move down the right allowed Kostoulas to tee up Ayari to sweep home via a deflection off the unfortunate Canvot. Sage looked like he wanted the ground to swallow him up.

If he hoped things might improve after the break then he was mistaken. It took Kostoulas only four minutes to make it 4-0 after the ball deflected into his path after good work from Gross. To the delight of the Brighton fans, Jean-Philippe Mateta contrived to hit the crossbar with the goal gaping on his return from injury before Eddie Nketiah also fluffed the chance to grab a consolation.

Sage’s assistant, Paddy McCarthy, had to be held back from confronting the Brighton bench, with tempers threatening to spill over. Plenty of Palace fans had already seen enough by then as they made their escape after a nightmarish afternoon. They missed Hinshelwood scoring from close range six minutes from the end to round off the perfect afternoon for Hürzeler, who could not hide his emotion as he celebrated with his players at full time.

Sports.title: European football: 10-man Lyon hold off Nice to move top of Ligue 1
Sports.content:
Ten-man Lyon held on for a 2-1 comeback victory over Nice to move top of Ligue 1 on Sunday, as previous pacesetters Monaco lost for the first time this season. Five teams are level on 14 points at the top of the table with Lyon heading Paris Saint-Germain, Paris FC, Lille and Monaco on goal difference.

It was a close run affair for Lyon, playing in front of local boy and French cycling prodigy Paul Seixas, following Keito Nakamura’s dismissal 20 minutes from time.

Côte d’Ivoire forward Elye Wahi, who opened the scoring for Nice on 18 minutes with his second goal of the season, was denied a stoppage-time equaliser by a tight offside call.

Two goals in three minutes turned the game around by half-time as Pavel Sulc equalised by prodding home a rebound and Tanner Tessmann headed the hosts in front.

Veteran Belgium midfielder Axel Witsel headed against the bar early in the second half while Wahi hit the post with a close-range header, shortly after Nakamura was dismissed for a high boot.

Noah Cadiou’s second-half penalty for Lorient prevented Monaco returning to the top of Ligue 1 as they fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.

Finnish goalkeeper Lukas Hradecky dived the right way, but Cadiou placed his spot-kick into the corner, to hand Monaco their first league defeat of the season.

Monaco are one of five teams level on points at the top of the table as they were joined by Paris FC, who edged Rennes 4-3 thanks to Lassine Sinayoko’s injury-time penalty. Rennes dropped to fifth, a point behind, despite forward Estéban Lepaul’s hat-trick of penalties in Paris.

Marseille picked up a much-needed win as they thumped Angers 5-2 to pull away from the relegation zone. Le Havre remain rooted to the foot of the table as Cameroon forward Danny Namaso’s double helped Auxerre come away from Normandy with a 3-1 victory.

View image in fullscreen Kylian Mbappé blasts home Real Madrid’s third goal. Photograph: Ángel Martínez/Getty Images

Kylian Mbappé scored ⁠twice as Real Madrid closed the gap on ⁠La Liga leaders ⁠Barcelona ​to six points with a 4-1 home win over ⁠Sevilla on Sunday, a week ⁠before the rivals meet in el clásico.

Arda Guler ​opened the ‌scoring in the ‌30th minute, arrowing a shot ‌into the top corner from outside the box, before Mbappé added a second seven minutes later after a brilliant turn. Mbappé ‌then won and converted a penalty in the 63rd minute ​to effectively settle the contest.

Sevilla pulled one back with 10 minutes remaining through the substitute Manu Bueno, ⁠but Yan Diomandé restored Real’s three-goal ​lead ​with a thunderous ​strike two minutes later.

An early penalty from Ante Budimir and a late Asier Osambela goal from earned Osasuna a 2-0 win against Racing Santander while Celta Vigo won 2-1 at home against Alavés.

Ibrahim Maza and Patrik Schick combined to score two goals as Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to beat in-form Freiburg 2-1 in the Bundesliga on Sunday.

After a shock defeat to promoted Elversberg in the season opener, Leverkusen have now picked up 13 of a possible 18 points and sit fourth, level with third-placed Freiburg – who host Bayern Munich next weekend – on points.

Rock bottom Borussia Mönchengladbach are still searching for a first point of the season after losing 2-1 at home against fellow strugglers Hoffenheim.

Hoffenheim’s Bambasé Conté opened the scoring with his second goal in two games since a surprise call-up to the Germany squad in October. Wael Mohya levelled for the hosts just after the break, but Alexander Prass put Hoffenheim back in front shortly afterwards as the visitors, who host Lyon in the Europa League on Thursday, won just their second game of the season.

View image in fullscreen Patrik Schick scores Bayer Leverkusen’s winner. Photograph: Martin Meissner/AP

Lazio’s Danish duo made the difference in Turin as Oliver Provstgaard and Gustav Isaksen ⁠scored in a 3-0 ⁠win over ​Juventus on Sunday that lifted their side level with Inter at the top of Serie A.

Provstgaard broke the deadlock in the ⁠37th minute, using his height to glance home Mattia Zaccagni’s cross after Lazio worked a short corner on the left.

Fellow Dane Isaksen doubled the lead in ⁠the 66th minute, collecting a pass from Nuno Tavares on the right before shifting the ball onto ​his left foot and bending a low ‌finish into the far ‌corner.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru completed the scoring in the 89th minute, launching a counterattack from inside his own ‌half and driving into the box before slotting home a low finish as frustrated home supporters jeered their side through to the final whistle.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como ended their three-game winless streak in Serie A on Sunday with a 3-1 victory at lowly Fiorentina.

First-half goals by Mattia Liberali and Nico Paz put the visitors in charge, before Marin Pongracic halved the deficit shortly before the interval. Anastasios Douvikas netted early in the second period to put to bed any hope of a Fiorentina comeback and keep the hosts locked in the relegation zone on four points.

Milan leapfrogged Como into fourth as they survived a second-half comeback from Atalanta to win 3-2. Goals from Gonçalo Ramos, Adrien Rabiot and Mario Gila put Milan 3-0 ahead after 58 minutes before Atalanta rallied through Gianluca Gaetano and Nikola Krstovic.

Earlier, Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese, with Kialonda Gaspar, Konan N’Dri and Jamil Siebert all finding the net.

Sports.title: James and Carpenter lead Chelsea surge as sorry Spurs hit for six in WSL again
Sports.content:
Two goals each from a rampant Lauren James and battling Ellie Carpenter helped Chelsea to cruise past Tottenham and keep the pressure on Manchester City at the top of the Women’s Super League.

It was a thrilling statement from the home team, in a game laden with stunning goals after a first half in which Tottenham more than held their own.

James’s first was cancelled out by Matilda Vinberg approaching half‑time, before Carpenter restored Chelsea’s lead and James added her second. Sjoeke Nüsken and Maika Hamano, on as substitutes, powered in the fourth and fifth before Carpenter completed the rout.

On the impact of her substitutes Sonia Bompastor, the Chelsea head coach, said: “When it happens like that, the fact that they have clarity on what we expect from them, they have clarity on what the team is trying to achieve, and also they are coming with confidence, is always a positive.”

Following Tottenham’s 6-1 defeat by London City Lionesses this month Martin Ho said he was the “most frustrated” he has been during his time at the club. At Stamford Bridge it looked initially like it would be a different story after a strong start, only for the concession of the opening goal to provide a reminder of their defensive issues. Toko Koga was uncharacteristically caught out, the Japan defender being dispossessed by James who drove towards the near post before firing in from the tightest of angles.

View image in fullscreen Lauren James squeezes in Chelsea’s opener from the tightest of angles. Photograph: John Walton/PA

The bright play of Ho’s team did not evaporate, though, with Kadeisha Buchanan on hand to steer the ball out for a corner just ahead of Cathinka Tandberg. A deserved equaliser arrived just before the break when Vinberg converted Julie Blakstad’s pinpoint ball towards the far post with a bullet header.

If there was hope that Spurs would end their run of 20 WSL games against big four opposition without a win, enduring 16 defeats in that time, they were crushed in the second half.

“The first 60 minutes, I can take a lot from,” Ho said. “There’s a lot of good performances, a lot of the things we asked, they’ve done in abundance. I couldn’t have asked any more in that first 60 minutes.

Quick Guide WSL roundup: City hold off Brighton to maintain 100% record Show Manchester City held off a spirited fightback from Brighton to close out a 3-2 win and maintain their perfect start in the Women’s Super League. Andree Jeglertz’s side raced into a 3-0 lead after an early double from Khadjia Shaw and a first goal for summer signing Niamh Charles. Brighton, though, rallied before the break with goals from Olivia Garcia and Caitlin Hayes. City remain two points ahead of Chelsea. London City Lionesses made it a full house for the top three, beating Everton 2-1. First-half goals from Delphine Cascarino and England winger Freya Godfrey had seemingly put the Lionesses in control. Everton, though, set up a tense finish after substitute Holly McNamara headed in with 20 minutes left. Manchester United are up to fifth in the table after a third successive league win, seeing off bottom side Charlton 3-1. Three goals in the opening quarter of an hour saw Ella Toone and Andrea Medina put United two up before Leah Davidson pulled one back. Julia Zigioitti Olme completed the scoring just after the half-hour mark. Aston Villa stunned faltering Liverpool, coming from behind to secure a 2-1 win for their first league success of the season. Natalia Ramos scored a spectacular early opener, but Villa improved after half-time, with Chasity Grant firing in an equaliser before a Grace Fisk own goal. Kelly Gago scored the only goal in the first half as West Ham defeated Crystal Palace 1-0. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

“When you’re on top and you concede that second, the way we conceded, from our possession, then that deflates you maybe as a group a little bit. But we have to recover quickly psychologically.”

It was not so much a Spurs collapse as Chelsea putting their foot on the gas, channelling any anger and frustration felt at a less than dominant first-half performance into one full of gut-busting intensity in the second half. Just before the hour Bompastor’s side retook the lead, when Alyssa Thompson surged into the penalty area from the left before sending an angled cutback for the arriving Carpenter to power in.

Four minutes later James extended their lead, collecting the ball from Lucy Bronze in the centre circle before she powered towards goal, wrongfooted Koga and curled an effort past Lize Kop.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea retake the lead in the second half thanks to Ellie Carpenter’s first goal. Photograph: John Walton/PA

“It’s a big help when you have a player who can create from nothing,” Bompastor said of James. “I’m pleased, but I want to highlight the team performance. When the individuals are performing it’s because the team is performing as well and the players around her are doing the job for her to express her quality on the ball.”

Chelsea’s fourth was equally as stylish; Keira Walsh flicked the ball to Nüsken and she blasted a rising strike home six minutes after coming on.

Hamano found herself in acres of space for the fifth, sending a curling shot into the top corner. Walsh was at fault for Spurs’ late second, waiting too long to receive a pass which Gaupset pounced on and then fired a low effort past Hannah Hampton. Unwilling to let the game finish on a down note, Carpenter swapped the ball from her left foot to her right as she turned and fired in her second.

It was a chaotic finish to an end‑to‑end match, as Chelsea continue to assert their status as serious title contenders.

Sports.title: Evanilson swivels his hips to seal Bournemouth win against 10-man Sunderland
Sports.content:
Bournemouth’s, and Marco Rose’s, wait for a Premier League win is over. Sunderland, locked in the bottom three, are becoming this season’s object lesson in travelling too far, too fast.

Once Kevin Danso was dismissed in the 17th minute for the denial of a goalscoring opportunity, Sunderland were sunk. If Evanilson was the match-winner with a goal, an assist and as the player Danso fouled, Régis Le Bris’s team were architects of their own downfall. “A bad day, a bad start,” the Sunderland manager said. Sixth and seventh last season, both teams have struggled domestically while cruising in the Europa League but Sunderland’s troubles deepened.

There was mitigation on offer. With a tight turnaround from Leiria on Thursday, England’s south coast on Sunday and Poznan in midweek, Wearside resources are stretched and their European dream comes against uncomfortable domestic realities. Talk of a possible sale continues, a boardroom reshuffle placing Kyril Louis-Dreyfus, the youthful majority owner, in charge of day‑to‑day operations. On the pitch, Sunderland have not had a league win since August, and lost four in succession.

Both teams had made five changes from Thursday and Bournemouth, who had beaten Sturm Graz at home, were visibly fresher. “Fatigue for me is not an issue,” Le Bris said. “We just have to get used to it.”

Granit Xhaka’s early stumble prefaced a jet-lagged, error-strewn performance that followed Sunderland’s first European away game since 1973. After Lewis Cook dabbed the ball forward, Evanilson seized on a collective muddle between Danso and Omar Alderete. The Brazilian’s reputation for unselfishness was deepened by his next choice of action. Instead of shooting, he laid up a diving Marcus Tavernier to head home. “I was waiting for him to shoot but he can see more than you and me,” Rose said.

“Exactly the situation we wanted to avoid,” Le Bris said, and Danso’s exit swiftly made things worse. Evanilson again escaped beyond a dallying defender exposed by Alderete ducking away from the ball. Clumsiness served as no defence. Craig Pawson, the referee, could reach no decision other than sending the Austrian for an early sachet of shower gel.

View image in fullscreen Marcus Tavernier points the way after scoring Bournemouth’s first goal. Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/Reuters

Being a goal and a man up represented a challenge to Bournemouth; they had previously conceded nine points from winning positions. First‑half chances piled up, Robin Roefs repeatedly asked to bail out bungling defenders. “If you have one player more you have to use the momentum,” Rose said.

With pressure piling on, the season lurching, Le Bris can only fight with the players available. Brian Brobbey, on the bench in Portugal following injury on international duty, was missing altogether from the matchday squad. “We decided not to rush the process,” Le Bris said. Timur Tutierov, loaned last season to Exeter, chased autumnal shadows before a merciful substitution on 59 minutes.

On the sidelines Rose, who revealed last week that he had binge‑watched Sunderland ’Til I Die on Netflix, kicked every ball. His need for three points was implicit. With the Vitality Stadium modernising fast, fans sitting in new-build corner stands, relegation battles cannot be countenanced. The second goal was accompanied by a collective sigh of relief, arriving via more Sunderland benevolence. Evanilson, assisted by Alderete’s brain-fog backpass, supplied a hip swivel of which Rudolf Nureyev might have been proud, sitting Roefs down to slot into an empty net. “I am happy that he rewarded himself with a goal,” Rose said of his No 9. “He is always working hard for the team.”

View image in fullscreen Kevin Danso brings down Evanilson before being shown a red card by referee Craig Pawson. Photograph: David Klein/Reuters

Bournemouth signed off with 29 shots. If thoughts understandably drifted to Thursday and Milan, seven-time European champions, coming to Dorset, Rose would not allow his players to be distracted. Though Sunderland enjoyed a late, brief spell of pressure, Bournemouth calmly collected a win that capped a historic week in club history. “It felt very clear, after [the 5-1 defeat on Friday against] Chelsea we were waiting for this game,” Rose said. “I am settling in well, I love the region. It’s a pleasure to work here. Everyone here stays patient and I really appreciate it.”

For Le Bris, any European success will only be a sticking plaster. “It’s hard to fix without a specific pattern,” he said, lamenting many mistakes. “It wasn’t the best version of Sunderland.”

Two clubs facing similar challenges appear on different trajectories.

Sports.title: Scottish Premiership: Osmand and Nygren at the double as Celtic thrash Hearts 7-1
Sports.content:
Callum Osmand was on target again as Celtic inflicted more misery on Hearts with a 7-1 thrashing at Parkhead.

Osmand netted twice in three first-half minutes in the first meeting of the teams since his goal sealed Celtic’s last-gasp title success at the expense of the Edinburgh side.

The Hoops were two up inside 10 minutes after Kieran Tierney and Benjamin Nygren both scored from Mika Baur corners, and the latter had the Premiership champions 5-1 up at the interval after forcing an own goal from Jamie McCart.

Camilo Durán piled on the agony with a goal four minutes after the restart and Nygren rounded off the scoring to send Martin O’Neill’s side four points clear of Rangers.

Hearts had arrived in Glasgow as the division’s top goalscorers and with the opportunity to move two points behind the leaders.

They produced 20 shots at goal, one of which found the net from Laurent Mendy, but Celtic were far superior in the final third and benefited from some extremely slack defending.

Rangers passed up the chance to go top of the Premiership in a pulsating 2-2 draw against Dundee at Dens Park on Saturday. The home side took a deserved lead in the 38th minute through the striker Bradley Fink but the returning Gers attacker Badredine Bouanani fired in a stunning equaliser three minutes later with his first goal for the club.

Derek McInnes’s side came out re-energised for the second half and took the lead on the hour with the midfielder Nico Raskin’s long-range drive but in the 68th minute the midfielder Callum Jones took advantage of Gers slackness to level. Dundee were well worth a point.

View image in fullscreen Bradley Fink gives Dundee the lead against Rangers from close range. Photograph: Andrew Milligan/PA

Greg Kiltie scored twice to lift Kilmarnock off the bottom with a 3-2 home victory over Motherwell. Kiltie struck first and last as Neil McCann’s side inflicted a fifth consecutive defeat on the Steelmen, who join Killie in the bottom three, one point above bottom-placed Hibernian.

Motherwell had a dominant spell after recovering from Kiltie’s second-minute opener and goals from Alex Lowry and Seb Palmer-Houlden turned the game on its head. But Tyreece John-Jules soon equalised and Motherwell were cut open before Kiltie knocked home a 69th-minute winner.

Motherwell’s manager, Alfred Johansson, bemoaned his side’s defending, saying: “I’m very, very disappointed and frustrated with how we end this game. It’s extremely difficult to accept the fact that we lost this game. We have chances to score more than two goals but we can’t rely on scoring three goals away from home. We need to be much more solid. It’s just way too low a level, how we defend.”

Falkirk secured an entertaining 2-1 win at Hibernian. Their only other league victory this term was at home to Hearts in September.

In a game that went from end to end, Jacob Murrell put Falkirk 2-0 ahead inside 37 minutes, before Hibs struck back with an Owen Elding goal. The home side dominated the second half, but could not bag an equaliser.

Aberdeen returned to winning ways as a 3-1 victory over St Mirren moved them above their opponents, who have now lost five straight matches. Brad Lyons gave the hosts the lead in spectacular fashion after two minutes, but the Buddies went on to dominate the first half and levelled through Eseosa Sule. In a much-improved second-half display strikes from Kevin Nisbet and Ayoub Mouloua gave the Dons three points. Aberdeen are seventh.

Lyall Cameron’s 79th-minute strike earned Dundee United a 1-1 draw at St Johnstone. United trailed at half-time to a Josh Fowler goal, the striker’s sixth of the Premiership campaign. The league’s top scorer did not make it out for the second half due to illness and Simo Valakari’s side were unable to repeat the trick of last Sunday in Aberdeen when they successfully defended a 1-0 lead.

Jim Goodwin had too many creative and attacking options to throw at their hosts and despite a decent defensive stand from the hosts, Cameron struck the second goal of his impressive loan spell from Rangers. The clubs are locked together on 12 points in the top half of the table after encouraging starts to the campaign, with the Saints in fifth on goal difference.

Sports.title: Martínez back ‘in a few weeks’ after jaw surgery; Liverpool lose Szoboszlai for ‘some time’ – matchday live

From 16h ago 03.14 EDT Martinez back 'in a few weeks' after jaw surgery Chelsea goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez said he would be fit to return “in a few weeks” following surgery on a fractured jaw sustained during his team’s 2-0 Premier League win at Everton. The Argentina international was taken to hospital after colliding with Everton defender Jarrad Branthwaite during the second half of Saturday’s game at Hill Dickinson Stadium. Martínez, 34, required eight minutes of treatment on the pitch before he was carried off on a stretcher. Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso later said he had suffered a concussion. “Thanks to everyone for the messages. The operation went well,” Martínez wrote on social media on Sunday alongside a photo of himself in a hospital bed. “The most important thing is that we won, and kept a clean sheet. We’ll be back in a few weeks.” Mike Penders is set to deputise in Martínez’s absence. The 21-year-old made his Premier League debut as a substitute against Everton. He joined from Belgian club Genk in August 2024 and has spent the past two seasons out on loan, including a spell at Strasbourg last term. 12h ago 07.25 EDT Donald McRae “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” But there’s sadness, too, in the way his life and career were scarred by his refusal to wear the poppy when playing games around Remembrance Sunday in England. “It’s completely changed me as a person,” McClean says. “It’s made me a bit of a recluse because I don’t trust a lot of people now. I’ve been stung bad.” McClean’s autobiography, The Walls, is one of the best sports books of the year. It’s a powerful and sometimes disturbing read elevated by McClean’s willingness to show himself in an unflattering light. 14h ago 04.48 EDT From the archive: Leeds United v Man Utd classics double quotation mark Leeds United 1-0 Manchester United (FA Cup semi-final replay, 31 March 1965); Leeds United 0-1 Manchester United (Division One, 17 April 1965) Here’s where the stags really begin to rut. Don Revie’s side, freshly promoted, were on course for the Double. Only problem was, so were Matt Busby’s men. The pair were drawn in the semi-final of the FA Cup, and spent 90 minutes at Hillsborough kicking seven colours out of each other, Jack Charlton, Billy Bremner, Nobby Stiles, Denis Law and Paddy Crerand enjoying themselves like the proverbial pigs. Good luck if you found yourself in the middle of that. Brouhahas broke out on the terraces as well, and did so again four days later during the replay at the City Ground. The on-field behaviour was much improved, though. According to Big Jack, Manchester United put on a performance as stylish and dangerous as they ever were under Busby, but Leeds somehow held on, wrested the ascendency, and nicked it in the last minute, Bremner twisting in mid-air to steer home an outrageous curling header. Bremner was missing 18 days later when Manchester United came to Elland Road in the league. Had they won, Leeds would have gone five clear at the top with four games left. They went into the game as favourites, Busby’s side having failed to find the net against Leeds in both Cup games and the earlier league match at Old Trafford, which the visitors won 1-0. That particular lean spell ended after 14 minutes – or 284, if you like – when John Connelly drove home. Leeds failed to respond, despite the best efforts of the newly crowned Football Writers’ player of the year, Bobby Collins, and went down again in their next Bremner-less match, a 3-0 hosing at Sheffield Wednesday. Busby’s third great side won their first title; Revie’s team, not quite ready yet, lost the Cup final as well. 15h ago 04.21 EDT Dominic Booth If the 2013 FA Cup final represented a blip for the Sheikh Mansour-era Manchester City in their quest for total domination of English football, it was a historic moment for their conquerors, Wigan Athletic. Memories of that famous day at Wembley still endure for Latics’ supporters despite the relegation from the Premier League that followed. Yet watching the modern-day Wigan, who remain bottom of League One despite a 1-0 win over Reading on Saturday, makes the toppling of City in a Cup final seem an epoch ago. The club, perhaps understandably, continue to hark back to their halcyon days. Last season they brought back Gary Caldwell – club captain in 2013 – for his second stint as manager, having led the club to promotion from this division in 2015-16. Choosing to swap Exeter for a return to the Latics last season was seen as a risky move by Caldwell, considering the shoestring budget imposed upon him by Mike Danson, the owner who is keen to sell. Finances are ultra-tight at the Greater Manchester club amid dwindling crowds and losses on the pitch and on the balance sheet. The local businessman Danson and his family saved Wigan from liquidation in June 2023 after mismanagement from previous owners brought a points deduction and relegation from the Championship. Three successive mid-table finishes in League One under their stewardship have brought a semblance of stability, but this season they have plummeted. The problem is the Dansons have been unable to find an ambitious buyer to take the club to the next level. Now the prospect of a first season in the fourth tier since 1996-97 is a distinct possibility, although victory against Reading – the Latics’ second league win of the campaign, sealed by Scott Hogan’s 71st-minute strike – made the picture a little rosier. Wigan pine for FA Cup glory as not even victory can lift them off foot of League One Read more Share

16h ago 03.28 EDT Jonathan Wilson The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” This was everything Sunderland fans could have wished for from their first European away game in 53 years and more. They had seen other fans experience these things, and now they could tick off the checklist: complicated travel to a pretty foreign town they would otherwise never visit, a fussy Albanian referee and a great sense of togetherness and community. There was even an injury-time winner from, miracle of miracles, Noah Sadiki. Ask any of the 5,000 or so Wearsiders who made the trip to Portugal if the Europa League was worth it and the answer would be unanimous. Bournemouth, Crystal Palace and Brighton fans would surely say something similar: European football, especially for clubs who are unfamiliar with it, is a joy and an adventure. It generates experiences that will be remembered for ever, and if the cost is that the risk of relegation goes up, that’s a price worth paying. Others at those clubs may see things differently. Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson Read more Share
