Sports.title: Russell and Leclerc are the joint ‘sprint race champions’ of 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Andrea Kimi Antonelli can clinch the drivers’ championship at the next round – but three of his rivals out-scored him over the course of Formula 1’s six sprint races this year.

Singapore played host to F1’s sixth and final sprint race of 2026 last weekend. The sprint races were won by four different drivers: George Russell won three (Shanghai, Montreal and Zandvoort), while his team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli triumphed at Silverstone, Lando Norris won in Miami and it was Max Verstappen’s turn in Singapore.

Russell could have beaten Verstappen last weekend, of course, having taken the lead off him at the start. But his crash at the end of lap one ended his chances of winning a fourth sprint race.

It also meant he ended the year with as many sprint race points as a driver who didn’t win any of these races. Charles Leclerc collected 34 points from sprint races, the same as Russell. This was made possible by the single-point gaps between finishing positions in sprint races, which are much closer than those used in grands prix.

After Russell’s retirement, Norris was on course to end the year as the top sprint race points-scorer. But his last-lap tangle with his team mate cost him three points and left him third.

As points are only awarded to the top eight finishers in sprint races, the drivers from the top four teams tended to monopolise them, with one exception: Isack Hadjar did not score a single point in a sprint race.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Liam Lawson scored points for both Red Bull (while substituting for Hadjar at Zandvoort) and Racing Bulls in sprint races. His regular team mate Arvid Lindblad also took sprint race points, as did Alpine’s Pierre Gasly and Audi’s Nico Hulkenberg.

But for almost half the grid, the sprint races offered nothing. The addition of four more sprint races next year could further increase the gap between the leading teams and the midfield.

IndyCar champion and Indianapolis 500 winner Dan Wheldon lost his life in a horrific crash in the season finale at Las Vegas 15 years ago today.

Sports.title: Singapore victory leaves Verstappen one win away from a full set – but not for long | 2026 Singapore Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen’s 73rd career victory was surely one of the most overdue of his career. At his 10th attempt, the Red Bull driver finally won the Singapore Grand Prix.

He’d come close several times before. Verstappen had started second four times and converted three of those into second-place finishes. On the other occasion he was wiped out by the Ferrari drivers as they sprinted to turn one.

But after finally claiming his first pole position at the Marina Bay circuit, Verstappen never let go of his advantage, leading every lap of the race. However with other drivers switching to the preferred soft tyres over the final stint, Verstappen did not set the fastest lap, so he did not collect his seventh ‘grand slam’.

He has now won at 27 different circuits, a feat only bettered by Lewis Hamilton on 31. Verstappen has won on every track on the calendar with a single exception: the Madring, which held its first grand prix this year.

However in order to complete a clean sweep of victories at every track on the calendar, Verstappen will have to win at three new rounds next year. Two venues where he has raced in F1, but not previously won at, will return on the 2027 F1 calendar.

What’s more, another driver will be in the same position as Verstappen. This is Hamilton, the last driver to have achieved a clean sweep:

Hamilton last achieved a clean sweep when he won the French Grand Prix in 2018. He kept up the achievement over the next two seasons – even as the Covid-19 pandemic added new races to the schedule in 2020 – but his run ended when he failed to win at Zandvoort in 2021.

Achieving a clean sweep next year would arguably be a greater feat for either driver. There were 21 circuits on the calendar when Hamilton achieved it in 2018, but there are 24 on next year’s schedule.

Verstappen became the fifth driver to achieve 50 pole positions last weekend. He did so in his 250th race start and joins Ayrton Senna, who took 108 races to do the same, Hamilton (168), Michael Schumacher (177) and Sebastian Vettel (196).

This was the fourth year in a row the Singapore Grand Prix has been won from pole position. Verstappen led every lap on his way to victory, which is the fourth ‘lights-to-flag’ victory at the circuit in the last five years, along with Sergio Perez’s win in 2022 (from second on the grid), Carlos Sainz Jnr’s in 2023 and Lando Norris’s from 2024.

Red Bull was only one win behind Mercedes when the season began. However Mercedes has enjoyed such a strong season that Red Bull’s victories in the last two rounds means its is now 10 behind. However Red Bull did end Mercedes’ streak of leading at least one lap in every race this year.

Racing Bulls reached 100 points, which is more than they scored last year and their best score since 2021, when they competed as AlphaTauri.

10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Robert Garcia Questions Unequal Protection On Canelo Alvarez Card
Sports.content:
Robert Garcia wants assurances about his camp’s safety before Lindolfo Delgado’s October 31 vacant IBF light welterweight title fight in Riyadh. He expects Canelo Alvarez to receive royal treatment ahead of his fight with Christian Mbilli, but fears his own team will be left traveling without the same protection.

The veteran trainer sounded uneasy rather than defiant when speaking on his team’s travel logistics. His issue is not whether the bout takes place, but the wide gulf between how the headliner travels and how the undercard talent gets moved into Saudi Arabia.

Canelo operates in an entirely different financial stratosphere. Garcia expects him to arrive by private plane with security handling his trip to the arena. His fear is that Delgado and his corner will have to fly commercial and pass through a public airport without comparable protection.

“They’ll f***ing fly private. They’ll go into a private airport where nobody knows where they’re at. They’ll have security driving them to the arena,” Garcia told Elie Seckbach.

Garcia wants similar protection for his group, but his tone sounded more resigned than demanding. He knows how big-money boxing operates. Promoters spare no expense for the box-office anchor, while supporting fighters are left to fend for themselves on standard itineraries.

“Canelo’s fight might happen because, like I told you, he’s secured. Not us. We’re not secured,” Garcia admitted.

The idea of Delgado’s camp joining Canelo on a private charter is wishful thinking, and Garcia practically acknowledged it in the same breath.

“If they tell us, ‘You guys are all traveling together,’ then we’re fine, but I don’t think that’s the case.”

Garcia doesn’t sound hopeful. Delgado is fighting Artur Biyarslanov for the vacant IBF light welterweight title, but that doesn’t buy him Canelo’s treatment. Canelo headlines the event. Delgado fills a spot underneath him, even with a world championship at stake.

Robert can vent to reporters, but walking away could cost his fighter the opportunity he’s been working toward. If Garcia refuses to travel without better security, organizers could look for a replacement. Delgado would then be watching somebody else fight for the belt.

That’s what makes Garcia’s position so uncomfortable. He has every reason to ask how his team will be protected, yet Delgado could be the one paying for it if they refuse to go. A world title shot is a powerful incentive to board the plane, even when your trainer has serious doubts about the trip.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley’s Defeats Overshadow His Finest Boxing Year
Sports.content:
A back-and-forth heavyweight fight captures the public’s collective imagination like few other sporting events. Countless expressions originating or popularized in heavyweight boxing describe competitive sporting events. “A knockdown drag-out contest”, “teams throwing haymakers”, “a slugfest”, “a heavyweight fight”, and many other such phrases regularly feature on football, baseball and basketball broadcasts.

The first fight between Daniel Dubois (24-3, 23 KO) and Fabio Wardley (20-2-1, 19 KO) in May illustrated the fantasy of what many envision in a heavyweight clash. Knockdowns, temerity, mettle, blood, violence. In the end, Daniel Dubois prevailed via technical knockout in the eleventh round. Fabio Wardley lost his championship, but gained the respect of anyone watching. It instantly entered the “fight of the year” conversation and was hailed as a heavyweight classic.

…

This past Saturday, just over five months later, Dubois and Wardley met again. The rematch was anticlimactic by comparison. The fight featured an early knockdown like the first encounter, though this time Daniel Dubois delivered it. Though Wardley tried to resist Dubois’ onslaught, it proved to be futile. Dubois nearly ended the bout inside the first round. But Wardley survived long enough to hear the bell to conclude round one. Ultimately, Wardley’s doggedness just lengthened his suffering.

Sixty seconds later, as round two began, Dubois was patient, waiting to find openings to pound away at Wardley. Dubois did it in short order. In the final minute of round two, Dubois peppered a winded and wounded Wardley with clean, powerful punches. The fight got stopped 2:21 into the second round; it was undoubtedly a fair stoppage. Referee Steve Gray stopped the contest just as Wardley’s trainer Ben Davidson threw in the towel from the corner.

Dubois obliterated Fabio Wardley and extinguished any doubt from fans and media, at least for now.

…

Fabio Wardley was a latecomer to boxing, turning professional at 22 years old with no amateur fights on his resume. Both his age and lack of amateur experience are considered rarities. Four fights into his pro career, Wardley agreed to be managed by Dillian Whyte, a fellow British heavyweight and former sparring partner. Wardley was born in Ipswich, England, and naturally is a lifelong supporter of Ipswich Town Football Club. He attained a dream by fighting at Ipswich Town’s stadium, Portman Road, in June 2025. His knockout win there over Justis Huni helped propel Wardley to recognition as 2025’s British Boxer of the Year, according to multiple outlets. An upset victory over former world champion Joseph Parker earned Wardley the WBO’s interim heavyweight championship. Wardley’s banner year of 2025 set him up to challenge Daniel Dubois in May for the vacant WBO heavyweight title.

…

On Saturday, Fabio Wardley was walloped. This year, Wardley has zero wins and two losses, both by technical knockout. But boxing fans will always remember the slugfest Wardley and Dubois had in May. While 2025 was Wardley’s most successful year in boxing, he will inevitably be associated with Daniel Dubois and their classic fight five months ago. In a career in which he has beaten former world champions and scored devastating knockouts, boxing fans will most fondly remember Fabio Wardley for a fight he lost.

It might not be fair, but it is reality. In a way, it is endearing, though. Even if Fabio Wardley never competes for a heavyweight championship again, the Ipswichian has forever earned a place in heavyweight boxing lore for his performance on May 9, 2026.

…

Sports and society at large are infatuated with analytics and data. Decades from now, when a young boxing fan asks their personalized robot about Fabio Wardley, they will be unimpressed by consecutive knockout losses. But if that young fan finds an old head and mentions Fabio Wardley, they will hear about his toughness, how he could have won a title in a different era, who Wardley reminds them of, and whatever else. Wardley and Dubois have earned remembrance in highlight reels and recollections, the greatest accolade of all.

Sports.title: Dalton Smith Wants Shakur Stevenson After Alberto Puello
Sports.content:
Dalton Smith is already eyeing a massive unification bout with Shakur Stevenson, even with his first WBC light welterweight title defense against Alberto Puello just days away.

Smith (19-0, 14 KOs) meets Puello on October 24 at Utilita Arena Sheffield. The unbeaten titleholder wants this victory to catapult him toward marquee names. Shakur sits near the top of his target list, but Puello can ruin everything.

“I’m boxing to be a part of the biggest fights possible. Of course the Shakur fight would be up there as one of the biggest. I’d love to be a part of that,” Smith told the Boxing World YouTube channel. “But of course, I have to get through Puello first.”

Smith grabbed the WBC belt back in January by stopping Subriel Matias inside five rounds during his US debut. Blowing through Matias earned him huge momentum, though it guarantees nothing against Puello.

Puello brings an awkward southpaw style. Smith will not get the same gifts he received from Matias, who walked straight in until he got caught by heavy counters. Puello is far more than a tune-up on the way to a Shakur payday. This matchup tests whether Dalton can defend his crown against a completely different kind of opponent.

“I don’t overlook what’s in front of me, but once I get the job done against Puello, I want to be chasing the biggest fights possible,” Smith said.

Puello (25-1, 11 KOs) has his own motives to spoil the party and steal that massive future date for himself. Calling out Shakur is the easy part for Smith. He still has to leave the ring with the belt.

Even if he gets past Puello, Dalton is overlooking the obstacles that will prevent him from fighting Shakur next. The network and promotional divide makes the Shakur-Smith fight virtually impossible to assemble right now. Shakur is signed with Zuffa and locked into Paramount+, while Smith is a Matchroom flagship fighter tied to DAZN.

Dual-network broadcasts only happen when the revenue numbers are astronomical, like Gervonta Davis against Ryan Garcia or massive undisputed heavyweight cards funded by deep foreign pockets. Dalton Smith versus Shakur Stevenson is nowhere near that category.

Neither guy moves US pay-per-view buys on that scale, and Zuffa has zero incentive to share production, split domestic rights, or loan out Shakur to DAZN for an ordinary regular-subscription card.

Dalton is known almost exclusively in the UK, and Shakur has struggled to build an audience that translates into commercial event revenue.

Zuffa Boxing did not bring Shakur to Paramount+ just to farm him out to DAZN or hand Matchroom control of an international production. If Zuffa wants Shakur in a unification or a meaningful fight at 140 pounds, they have zero business justification to share the pie with an outside streaming rival on an event with minimal domestic pay-per-view appetite.

Sports.title: Terence Crawford, Tim Bradley Challenge Fundora Stoppage
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora’s last-second stoppage of Ermal Hadribeaj drew objections during a post-fight discussion involving Terence Crawford and Tim Bradley, while Dan Rafael called for the result to be changed to a decision.

Hadribeaj appeared able to continue when the referee halted Saturday’s fight in Las Vegas. The unusual ending put a cloud over Fundora’s WBC junior middleweight title defense, with the dispute focused on Hadribeaj beating the count after the final bell had already sounded.

“All he had to do was get on his feet,” came one objection during the discussion involving Crawford, Bradley and the referee.

The referee defended his intervention by pointing to Hadribeaj falling back into the ropes and arguing that another attack would have left him in trouble.

“If there’s five seconds left, that guy gets destroyed,” he said.

But those five seconds did not exist. That is the problem with using a possible follow-up attack to justify the stoppage. Hadribeaj had no more fighting left to do if he had beaten the count after the final bell.

Rafael made that argument forcefully on X, urging Hadribeaj’s team to protest to the Nevada State Athletic Commission.

“HE BEAT THE COUNT and the bell had already rung,” Rafael said. “Won’t be surprised at all if the NSAC changes the result to a unanimous decision.”

That was Rafael’s expectation, rather than an announced commission action. Still, his criticism gives Hadribeaj’s team a specific issue to raise: whether the referee improperly extended the process beyond the completed count when the fight had already ended.

This is about dollars and cents, not just hurt feelings. Getting tagged with an illegitimate knockout loss hurts Hadribeaj’s marketability and ruins his leverage for future paydays. Fundora keeps his win on the cards anyway, but the commission needs to step in, overturn the bogus stoppage, and take an undeserved KO loss off Hadribeaj’s record.

Sports.title: Filip Hrgovic Tells Moses Itauma: “No Time For Crying”
Sports.content:
Filip Hrgovic is having a grand time talking down to Moses Itauma. As the young heavyweight mopes over his first defeat and fixates on replays, Hrgovic delivered a blunt reality check: stop crying, get back in the gym, and figure out how to win when your opponent refuses to fall over.

Itauma admitted this week that rewatching the bout eats away at him. He landed his best artillery, watched Hrgovic walk straight through it, and kept winging power shots until his gas tank emptied completely. He sounds like a fighter in denial, still convinced the knockout was right there if he had just thrown a little harder.

Hrgovic responded with dripping condescension, offering to comfort the 21-year-old prospect like a disappointed toddler.

“I’ll tell him, ‘Look, Moses, everything will be good,'” Hrgovic told The Stomping Ground. “I will cuddle him … on the head, like, ‘Moses, everything will be good. Don’t be upset.'”

The mocking humor carried an unforgiving point. Hrgovic pointed out that a loss should light a fire under a fighter rather than shatter his nerve, before making sure to remind everyone who dismantled the hype train.

“You must learn from that that you can’t knock out Filip Hrgovic,” he said. “You must learn you can’t knock out everyone. You must be ready for a 12-round fight.”

That diagnosis is right on the money. Itauma got exposed by his own reliance on early blowouts. Once his power failed to create a shortcut, he had no Plan B, frantically emptying his reserves against an immovable target walking him down.

Surviving at the top level means knowing how to bank rounds without punching yourself into exhaustion. Itauma needs to accept that durable heavyweights will absorb his Sunday punch and keep coming.

Hrgovic threw in obligatory compliments about Itauma’s raw speed, but the core message was pure dismissal.

“No time for crying. Go back to the gym, and that’s it, man. Simple.”

Staring at the tape will not undo the beating. Itauma either learns how to box when the stoppage vanishes, or the next seasoned heavyweight will run the exact same script on him.

Sports.title: VIDEO: Daniel Dubois vs Fabio Wardley II – FIGHT REVIEW
Sports.content:
This past Saturday on the 17th of October, from The O2 Arena in London, England, in a championship rematch that was available live worldwide on DAZN PPV – reigning WBO heavyweight champion Daniel Dubois made an emphatic statement, stopping former titleholder Fabio Wardley in the 2nd round to successfully retain his championship.

Get DAZN Ultimate Tier HERE

The heavyweight division has been in total chaos ever since Oleksandr Usyk vacated his collection of alphabet belts, leaving the rest of the division battling for supremacy in a wide-open landscape. Entering the night, the big question was whether Wardley could make the necessary pacing adjustments after dropping Dubois twice early before being stopped in the 11th round of their first encounter five months ago. Instead, Dubois erased all doubt immediately and authored a destructive blowout.

Rather than another back-and-forth war of attrition, Dubois completely flipped the script from their first clash right out of the gate. In the opening seconds of round 1, Dubois caught Wardley flush with a booming shot that dropped the challenger hard to the canvas. Wardley beat the count, but he remained on unsteady legs for the rest of the frame. Staying cool, calm, and composed, Dubois patiently picked his spots and battered Wardley mercilessly before the bell.

Wardley came out for the 2nd round trying to establish his footing and survive the storm, but Dubois was completely dialed in. Stalking his hurt rival with authority, Dubois unleashed another heavy barrage of clubbing shots traps along the ropes, prompting Wardley’s corner to mercifully throw in the towel to save their fighter from further punishment.

This edition of Rummy’s Corner provides a full recap and post-fight review of Dubois’s dominant title defense, while exploring what could be next in the heavyweight division. This is Rummy’s Corner (written, narrated, and produced by Geoffrey Ciani).

Sports.title: “The Towering Inferno” Fundora Stops Hadribeaj in Final Round
Sports.content:
WBC super welterweight champion Sebastian “The Towering Inferno” Fundora stopped Ermal “The Albanian Sniper” Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the twelfth and final round of an action-packed but often sloppy fight at the Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas, Nevada.

Promoters Tom Brown of TGB Promotions and Sampson Lewkowicz of Sampson Boxing presented the card Saturday on DAZN and TNT.

In the main event, southpaw Fundora, 25-1-1 (17 KOs), of Coachella, California, stopped fellow southpaw Hadribeaj, 23-1-1 (8 KOs), of Tirana, Albania, and Miami Beach, Florida, at 2:59 of the final round.

In the second round, Fundora used his considerable height advantage to hurt Hadribeaj early. The challenger fought back and had Fundora in trouble near the end of the round. In the third, referee Thomas Taylor deducted a point from Hadribeaj for excessive holding.

There was nonstop action from the fourth through the tenth as Hadribeaj forced his way inside and Fundora answered with short punches. The challenger made it competitive, although Fundora held an overall edge and increasingly found success with his body attack.

In the eleventh round, Taylor deducted another point from Hadribeaj for holding. Despite his height disadvantage, the challenger continued trying to force the fight at close range.

In the closing seconds of the twelfth, Fundora dropped Hadribeaj with a left hand. Hadribeaj beat the count but was in no condition to continue, prompting Taylor to wave it off with one second remaining.

In the co-main event, former WBA super middleweight champion Armando “Toro” Resendiz, 17-3 (11 KOs), of Guayabitos, Mexico, defeated Koen Mazoudier, 16-5-1 (6 KOs), of Blacktown, New South Wales, Australia, by unanimous decision over ten action-packed rounds.

Resendiz rocked Mazoudier with a right hand to the chin in the final seconds of the fourth round, knocking him off balance. From the sixth through the ninth, Mazoudier pressed the action and fought his way back into the contest, giving the crowd plenty to cheer about while Resendiz continued landing the heavier punches.

In the final minute of the tenth, Resendiz hurt Mazoudier with a flurry of unanswered shots. The Australian survived to hear the final bell.

The scores were 98-92 and 97-93 twice. Harvey Dock was the referee.

In an eight-round super middleweight bout, Jaime Osuna, 12-0 (5 KOs), of Guerrero Negro, Baja California Sur, Mexico, won a majority decision over Cristian Cangelosi, 13-1-1 (5 KOs), of Palermo, Italy, and Brooklyn, New York.

Osuna suffered a cut over his right eye from a left hook in the third round, which Cangelosi took with his cleaner work.

In the fifth, Osuna rocked Cangelosi early as the fight developed into a slugfest. Cangelosi answered in the seventh, catching Osuna with a right hand to the chin in the closing seconds.

Both had their moments in the eighth and final round, fighting hard with the result still in doubt.

Two judges scored it 77-75 for Osuna, while the third had it even at 76-76. Robert Hoyle was the referee.

Super middleweight Marco “El Tiburon” Romero, 16-0 (14 KOs), of Olathe, Kansas, stopped Matias Ferreira, 8-4 (3 KOs), of Rosario, Uruguay, at 1:54 of the first round of their scheduled eight-round bout.

Ferreira landed a left hook midway through the opening round, but Romero countered with a right hand to the chin that dropped him onto the seat of his trunks. Referee Tony Weeks stopped the contest following the knockdown.

Jimmy Lennon Jr. served as the ring announcer.

The scheduled bout between Brandon Figueroa and Tomoki Kameda was canceled after Figueroa became ill following his weight cut. Figueroa was also stripped of his WBA featherweight title after failing to make the division limit.

Sports.title: Ennis vs. Kelly Winner Targeted By Sebastian Fundora
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora wants the Jaron Ennis–Josh Kelly winner next, but a potential Ennis fight comes with a financial obstacle: promoter Sampson Lewkowicz’s demand for a 50-50 purse split.

Fundora called for undisputed after stopping Ermal Hadribeaj with one second remaining in the 12th round. The WBC junior middleweight champion sounded ready to pursue the other belts, although agreeing on an opponent is only part of getting a unification made.

“Absolutely, let’s go for undisputed,” Fundora told DAZN when asked about facing the Ennis–Kelly winner. “We will break them down like we broke this guy, like the guy before that, before that, and before. We’ll keep breaking these guys down.”

Fundora (25-1-1, 17 KOs) had just completed his fourth successful title defense, wearing down Hadribeaj with short punches and sustained body work before dropping him with a left hand at 2:59 of the final round.

That performance supported his description of breaking opponents down. Hadribeaj made the early rounds competitive by crowding Fundora, but the champion gradually took over through his greater activity inside.

Getting Ennis into the ring could require a different kind of patience. Lewkowicz has called for an equal split for Fundora against Ennis, leaving the financial terms as something the camps would have to resolve if Ennis beats Kelly.

There is no agreement established by Fundora’s post-fight comments, nor do they show that Ennis has accepted or rejected those terms. The potential obstacle is whether an equal split becomes a firm condition or a starting position in negotiations.

Fundora has made his preference clear. If Ennis wins, the next question will be whether the promoters can find a price both sides accept and turn that undisputed ambition into a scheduled fight.

Tonight’s showing only hurts Fundora’s negotiating position. Needing until the final second of the twelfth round to finish a gritty but limited challenger like Hadribeaj showed the exact vulnerabilities that have always followed Fundora. He surrenders his 6’6″ frame, stays glued in the pocket, eats clean shots on the inside, and relies strictly on outlasting foes in a war of attrition.

Ghana News.title: Harry Styles debuts new track in memory of Liam Payne
Ghana News.content:
Harry Styles performed an unreleased song he wrote for his former One Direction bandmate Liam Payne.

The Grammy Award-winning star performed the track "What Is Enough" during his sold-out concert at Madison Square Garden on the second anniversary of Payne's death.

Styles is currently performing at the New York venue as part of a residency on his record-breaking Together, Together tour.

Addressing the packed crowd on Friday night, the singer paid tribute to Payne as a friend and someone he "wouldn't have been able to do this without".

As a spotlight shone over him, Styles made a moving speech, in which he honoured Liam Payne, who died two years ago after falling from a hotel balcony in Argentina.

"I feel incredibly lucky to get to play these shows here in New York, and this building means a lot to me," said the artist.

"There are so many people in my life, friends and people that I've worked with that I wouldn't have been able to do this without," he continued.

"And two years ago today, I lost one of those friends."

This was met with cheers from the audience, who were hearing What Is Enough for the first time.

Wearing a royal blue jumper with a red collar, the musician then urged fans to keep an eye out for and support each other.

"I'm sure a lot of you have been through similar things. I hope you haven't.

"But really, it's just about looking after each other."

He added that there were "so many more people who have touched my life in such special ways", thanking those who helped him get to where he is.

"I'm gonna play you a song I wrote for my friend about two years ago, if that's all right."

As he paused, passionate cheers and clapping could be heard from his fans.

The singer then began to play his guitar and perform What is Enough, which featured emotional and reflective lyrics.

As he sang out to the crowd, his band played a melodic accompaniment.

Sharing their reaction to Friday night's performance on Instagram, Harry Styles' fans described What is Enough as "beautiful".

Styles launched his solo career in 2017 after becoming a global star in One Direction.

His first album and single were both UK number ones, while his record Harry's House won a Grammy and a Brit Award after its release in 2022.

Ghana News.title: Obuasi SHTS abuse allegations: Reported cases rise to 19
Ghana News.content:
The number of students who have come forward with allegations of sexual abuse involving the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School has risen from 16 to 19, JoyNews Investigative Journalist Manasseh Azure Awuni has disclosed.

He said three additional students had reportedly come forward, adding to the cases uncovered during his investigation.

“From yesterday, my sources at the school told me the number has grown to 19. So way more names have come up, and it is likely there will be more, because some didn't give a report,” he said on JoyNews' The Probe on Sunday, October 18.

Speaking on Joy FM on Thursday, October 15, about his latest documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, Manasseh said the initial information he received concerned five students.

However, the number increased to 14 when he visited the school to investigate. Two more students subsequently came forward with similar allegations, bringing the number to 16 before the latest three cases emerged.

Manasseh said the latest allegations were particularly troubling because they followed a similar incident at the school in 2018, involving a senior housemaster who was dismissed.

“I've been to Obuasi twice. First in 2018, and this is my second time visiting Obuasi. The first visit was about allegations of sexual assault in the same school,” he said.

He explained that after returning from studies abroad, he received a message from a source at the school indicating that the situation had worsened and that attempts had been made to reach him while he was away.

According to Manasseh, the situation was more difficult to address this time because the allegations involved the headmaster, who occupies the highest position in the school's administrative structure.

He also expressed concern about what he described as widespread awareness of the allegations within the Obuasi community, including among members of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), despite an apparent reluctance to speak publicly.

The allegations against the headmaster, Zakaria Abdulai, remain subject to investigation.

Ghana News.title: Withdraw from Juaben chairmanship race or face disqualification – NDC tells Obuasi SHTS headmaster
Ghana News.content:
The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has directed the suspended headmaster of Obuasi Senior High Technical School, Zakaria Abdulai, to withdraw his bid for the party’s Juaben constituency chairmanship or face disqualification.

Deputy National Communications Director Julius Anthony disclosed the directive on JoyNews’ The Probe on Sunday, saying the party’s national leadership had communicated its position to Mr Abdulai.

“The party has directed: withdraw your attempts to contest for the chairmanship or be disqualified. That is the party’s position, well communicated to the headmaster,” he said.

Mr Anthony said the decision was informed by ongoing law enforcement investigations into the headmaster.

“Our rationale is simple: this person is currently being investigated by law enforcement agencies who essentially report to our government,” he explained.

Mr Abdulai, who also serves as the NDC’s Juaben constituency secretary, has come under scrutiny following a JoyNews investigation by Manasseh Azure Awuni into allegations of sexual harassment, assault and rape involving female students.

The documentary, Inside the Dreaded Headmaster’s Bungalow, also examined how authorities handled complaints against him.

On October 13, Education Minister Haruna Iddrisu directed the Ghana Education Service to suspend Mr Abdulai pending a full investigation.

The minister also requested the Criminal Investigation Department headquarters to investigate the allegations.

The documentary found that students, parents and teachers had submitted complaints to school management, education officials and other authorities before the suspension.

It raised questions about delays in investigating those complaints and alleged interventions by influential figures.

When contacted during the investigation, Mr Abdulai declined to comment on the allegations, citing ongoing police and GES investigations.

The allegations remain under investigation. Mr Anthony’s announcement sets out the party’s position on the headmaster’s bid for the chairmanship while those inquiries continue.

Ghana News.title: Serb player banned to 2050 for tennis match-fixing
Ghana News.content:
A player from Serbia has been given a 24-year suspension from tennis — one of the most severe punishments imposed by anti-corruption investigators outside of a lifetime ban — for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic, who reached a career-high world ranking of 1,338th in 2014, was charged with fixing six matches, including five in which he was competing.

The 29-year-old, who played on the lower rungs of the professional ladder, was also charged with attempting to fix a further six matches between 2022 and 2024.

Along with the match-fixing, the International Tennis Integrity Authority (ITIA) said Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players "as part of a corrupt network".

Players recruited by Milicevic have also been accused by the ITIA of match-fixing.

The severity of Milicevic's sanction is partly down to a lack of co-operation in the investigation.

The ITIA said he "did not engage" in the process despite seven separate attempts from the independent organisation to contact him.

Milicevic, who also received a £53,000 fine, cannot take part in the sport until his ban ends in October 2050, by which time he will be 53 years old.

While suspended, he is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.

In December, French player Quentin Folliot was banned for 20 years, after the ITIA discovered he was a central figure in a network of players operating on behalf of a match-fixing syndicate.

Foillot, who reached a career-high ranking of 488 in 2022, denied charges relating to 11 matches that took place between 2022 and 2024, including eight in which he played.

However, at a hearing, some 27 of the 30 charges against him, relating to 10 of the 11 matches, were upheld.

Ghana News.title: The Quiet Engine of Growth: Why the right legal structure is your Ghanaian MSMEs’ greatest scaling tool
Ghana News.content:
You started your business to sell a product, deliver a service, or solve a problem you understood better than anyone else. You did not start it to read the Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992), or to decode the finer points of the Ghana Enterprises Agency Act, 2020 (Act 1043). Yet the uncomfortable truth is that some of the most ambitious micro and small enterprises (MSMEs) in Ghana hit a ceiling not because their ideas failed, but because their legal identities could not keep up with their ambition.

Ghana’s MSME sector is the undisputed backbone of the economy. It accounts for over 90 per cent of all businesses and contributes roughly 70 per cent to national GDP. But a vast number still operate as sole proprietorships or informal partnerships, outside the structured regulatory framework that unlocks serious scale. The law does not force you to incorporate. But discretion is not the same as strategy. Here are seven reasons why the legal structure and regulatory classification you choose may be the single most consequential business decision you make, and how each one directly helps a micro or small company scale up.

Limited Liability: You Can Risk the Business Without Risking Your Home

The most fundamental legal decision is whether your business has a separate legal identity from you. In a sole proprietorship, popularly called a “one-man business”, it does not. You are the business. If a large order goes wrong, if a buyer refuses to pay, or if a contract dispute turns ugly, your personal savings, your family’s home in Kumasi, and your children’s school fees are all on the table. The same is true for a general partnership under the Incorporated Private Partnerships Act, 1962 (Act 152), where Section 16 makes every partner jointly and severally liable for the firm’s debts.

A Private Limited Company under the Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992), changes this. Section 7(2)(a) defines it as a company “which has the liability of its members limited to the amount unpaid on the shares respectively held by them”. The company is a separate legal person. For a micro entrepreneur in Accra or Takoradi, this is not an abstract legal nicety. It is what allows you to take the calculated risks that scaling requires: bidding for a larger contract, entering a new regional market, hiring more people without exposing everything you own. As the Office of the Registrar of Companies (ORC) itself puts it, incorporation “safeguards personal assets from business debts”.

Access to Finance: The Collateral Revolution You Are Currently Missing

Access to credit is the perennial complaint of the small entrepreneur. The Bank of Ghana has identified a staggering US$4.8 billion annual financing gap for MSMEs, with only about 35 per cent having access to bank financing and over 50 per cent completely shut out of formal credit. But the regulatory and legal framework has changed in your favour if you are positioned to use it.

The Collateral Registry, established under the Borrowers and Lenders Act, 2008 and reinforced by the 2020 Act (Act 1052), was the first of its kind in Africa. It allows MSMEs who lack traditional land or buildings to use movable assets, stock, receivables, vehicles, machinery, and tools of trade to secure credit. Between 2010 and 2025, the Registry recorded over 1.92 million secured transactions. But a sole proprietor operating informally cannot fully leverage this architecture. A registered company or a formalised enterprise with proper documentation is visible to lenders, can register security interests, and can access the venture capital ecosystem that the Venture Capital Trust Fund (VCTF) has built over two decades: 77 companies funded, over GHS 2 billion in leveraged capital, and more than 28,000 jobs created. Scaling is expensive. Scaling with the wrong legal identity makes it unnecessarily more expensive.

Government Support and MSME Classification: The Door Is Labelled, but You Need the Key

The Ghana Enterprises Agency (GEA), established under Act 1043, is the institutional home for MSME support in Ghana. Its objects are explicitly to “develop and implement national programmes aimed at encouraging and accelerating the growth of MSMEs” and to “strengthen the capacity and competitiveness of MSMEs”. But the support flows through classification. Under LI 2470, a micro enterprise is defined as having 1–5 employees and annual turnover below GH¢300,000; a small enterprise has 6–29 employees and turnover between GH¢300,000 and GH¢6 million.

Formalisation is the key that turns this classification into access. The GEA’s Business Advisory Centres and Business Resource Centres nationwide provide capacity building, access to funding, and eligibility for government- and donor-supported interventions, but the benefits of being a registered client are tied to formalisation. The BizBox Project, a partnership between GEA and the Mastercard Foundation, is targeting 250,000 young Ghanaians with training, start-up kits, and market linkages. An enterprise that has not registered its legal structure is not a participant in this framework. It is a spectator.

Procurement: The Local Content Door Is Opening, but Only for the Registered

The government is the largest buyer in the country, with annual public procurement expenditure estimated at $3.5 billion, accounting for about 11 per cent of GDP. The Public Procurement Act, 2003 (Act 663) provides for margins of preference for domestic goods and works, and the government has proposed a margin of preference of about 30 per cent for Ghanaian goods. The Public Procurement Authority has also developed low-value and minor procurement guidelines specifically to bring MSMEs, artisans, and craftsmen into the formal procurement record.

But eligibility is not automatic. A business without a legal identity and proper registration cannot bid for contracts, cannot provide the documentation required for tender evaluation, and cannot claim the preference margins that the law allows. For a small manufacturer in Kumasi or a service provider in Tamale looking to move from local clients to institutional buyers, the right legal structure is not a marginal benefit. It is the price of admission to a market that is deliberately being opened to you.

Investor Readiness: Why the Right Structure Is the Price of Admission

If your scaling plan involves bringing in equity from an angel investor, a venture fund, or even a strategic partner, the legal structure is not a detail. It is the first thing a serious investor’s lawyer will examine. A sole proprietorship has no shares to issue. A general partnership under Act 152 can bring in partners but cannot issue equity shares. Investors overwhelmingly prefer Private Limited Companies, and the Companies Act, 2019 (Act 992) provides a clean framework for share issuance and transfer, a due diligence architecture, and the governance standards that external capital requires.

The VCTF’s entire model is built on this premise: it invests in Venture Capital Finance Companies that in turn invest equity and quasi-equity in SMEs, because the Fund recognises that high-cost debt alone has led to an “inordinately high business mortality rate” among SMEs. The Ghana Alternative Market (GAX), launched in 2013 with VCTF’s support, was specifically designed to give growth-oriented companies access to long-term capital. For a micro or small company with genuine scale ambitions, the question is not whether the compliance burden of a company structure is worth it. The question is whether you can afford to be invisible to the capital that will fund your next stage of growth.

Perpetual Succession and Credibility: The Business That Outlives the Founder

A sole proprietorship dies with the proprietor. The ORC is explicit: the ownership of the business dies with the owner. A partnership dissolves when its partners change. A company under Act 992 enjoys perpetual succession: the entity continues to exist independently of its owners, and shares can be transferred without dismantling the business. This matters for scale in two concrete ways. First, it makes the business bankable and investable over a longer horizon; lenders and investors can underwrite an institution, not just a person. Second, it allows you to build a management team and a brand that is not inseparable from your own name. The ORC’s registration campaign across Ghana is built on this message: registration confers credibility, legal recognition, and the trust of customers and partners. Formalisation is a credibility signal, not just a compliance cost.

Tax Compliance and Regulatory Simplicity: The System Is Making It Easier, If You Are Inside It

The final reason is cumulative. The Ghana Revenue Authority has introduced a Modified Taxation Scheme (MTS) for micro, small, and medium enterprises in the informal sector. Eligible taxpayers with annual incomes up to GHS 500,000 can pay a flat 3 per cent tax and register and pay via a dedicated mobile app, with options for fixed quarterly payments or turnover-based taxation. The GRA is even proposing to extend the MTS to qualifying small limited liability companies with annual turnover up to GH¢750,000, aligning the simplified regime with the VAT registration threshold.

This is the regulatory state actively building a bridge for small businesses to formalise without being crushed by compliance designed for large corporations. But the bridge leads into the formal system. An enterprise that has not registered its legal structure and obtained the necessary identification a TIN, an ORC registration, a place on the GEA client register cannot walk across it. The law and the regulatory architecture are not obstacles to scale. They are the operating system on which scale runs. The first step is deciding to stand on it.

The Legal Bottom Line

The law does not require you to incorporate. It does not even require you to register as an MSME to trade. But the law draws a clear line between those within Ghana’s formal MSME framework and those outside it. Inside the line: limited liability under Act 992, priority access to the Collateral Registry and the VCTF ecosystem, eligibility for GEA programmes and BizBox, procurement preferences, investor readiness, perpetual succession, and the Modified Taxation Scheme. Outside the line: unlimited personal liability, invisible creditworthiness, and commercial contracts governed only by whatever bargaining power you can muster on your own.

For the micro and small entrepreneur in Ghana, the choice of legal structure is not a bureaucratic formality. It is the operating system on which every other scaling decision runs. The right structure will not make a bad business good. But the wrong structure will quietly cap a good business at the exact moment it is ready to grow. The law has built the ladder. The first step is deciding to stand on it.

*******

Kweku Hammond, Snr Sales & Marketing Consultant/Faculty - Nova Business School Africa

Ghana News.title: Real Madrid demand Tebas resign over Goebbels comparison
Ghana News.content:
Javier Tebas has had several past disputes with Real Madrid

Real Madrid have called for the "immediate resignation" of La Liga president Javier Tebas after he drew comparisons between the club's management and Nazi propaganda chief Joseph Goebbels.

Tebas said Real Madrid's communication and the use of its in-house TV channel "recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels".

Real Madrid have called the statement "deeply offensive" and "morally repugnant".

The club have also demanded that Tebas step down as both the head of the Spanish top flight and vice-president of the Spanish Football Association (RFEF).

"Real Madrid considers it absolutely intolerable and extraordinarily serious that someone holding two positions of utmost responsibility in Spanish football resorts to a comparison with the propaganda methods of the Nazi regime to discredit our club, its management and its television," the club said.

In a lengthy post published on X on Friday, Tebas said: "Real Madrid's management directs an orchestra of mouthpieces and Real Madrid TV leads the singing.

"Their score is always the same: select the plays that suit them, repeat the grievance, feed the suspicion, and point fingers at the enemies.

"That method recalls propaganda mechanisms exploited by Goebbels, Nazi Germany's minister of propaganda: systematic repetition, construction of an enemy, and subordination of facts to the narrative."

Tebas later said he was drawing comparison with "those propaganda techniques" and "not with an ideology".

Real Madrid rejected this clarification, saying it did not mitigate the "institutionally unworthy nature of his statements".

The club added: "These statements constitute yet another episode in the repeated attacks by Javier Tebas against Real Madrid, its president and its media outlets."

Last month, Tebas criticised Real Madrid for alleging a refereeing conspiracy against the club.

He has also been critical of Real and its president, Florentino Perez, in previous years after disagreeing with their plans to join a European Super League in 2021.

In 2025 he said Real had "lost their head" after the club sent a formal letter of complaint to the Spanish FA about officiating in the league.

Ghana News.title: Fatigued Zverev ‘overachieved’ by reaching Shanghai semis
Ghana News.content:
World number two Alexander Zverev said he "overachieved" at the Shanghai Masters by reaching the semi-finals, despite fatigue from his busy schedule.

The 29-year-old top seed exited in the last four on Saturday as Spaniard Alejandro Davidovich Fokina pulled off a surprise 5-7 6-4 6-3 win, only his second in eight meetings with Zverev.

Germany's Zverev, who is guaranteed to end the season as world number one, has had little opportunity to rest between the US Open, the Laver Cup, the Beijing Masters, and the Shanghai Masters.

"I feel like I've actually, in a way, maybe overachieved this week because of how much tennis I played," Zverev said.

"I carried a little bit of injury, I carried fatigue into the tournament, and I'm OK to lose to a player like this today.

Repeatedly exposed on the forehand side, Zverev surrendered his first break of the match to an exquisite backhand passing shot on the run as Davidovich Fokina took the semi-final to a deciding set.

Zverev was broken to trail 2-0 in the third set and could not recover control of the tie as the 25th seed advanced to his first ATP Masters 1000 final since 2022.

Having failed to replicate the performance which earned him a straight-set win over Alex de Minaur in the quarter-final, Zverev said he has struggled since his fourth-round win over Alexander Bublik went to a third-set tie-break.

"First, I'm not a robot; I'm a human being. I get tired," Zverev said. "After the US Open, I had one day off in total. I think I played a lot of tennis, which is very, very positive because that means I played well.

"I think even here I had tough matches. I personally feel like I was quite flat since the Bublik match, because I was losing energy.

"I played a phenomenal match against Alex de Minaur, but today I was flat. Even in the first set, even though I won the set, I was flatter; I was not reacting so well. I was returning quite badly.

"We're all human beings, even the best players in the world."

His semi-final defeat is a disappointing exception to a brilliant season for Zverev, who claimed the first Grand Slam title of his career at the French Open in June before winning a second at the US Open in September.

Davidovich Fokina will face fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar in the final on Sunday.

Ghana News.title: NPP demands publication of invoices for GH¢27m South Africa evacuation flights
Ghana News.content:
The Communications Director of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has challenged Foreign Affairs Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa to publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for three chartered flights used to evacuate Ghanaians from South Africa.

He says the documents are needed to establish the actual cost of the flights following claims that the government paid $750,000 for each aircraft.

Speaking at a press briefing on Sunday, October 18, Miracles Aboagye said documents released by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, including its response to a Right to Information (RTI) request dated September 18, 2026, and a report to Parliament's Foreign Affairs Committee, raised questions about the expenditure.

He said the documents showed that GH¢27,183,700 was spent on chartered flights, representing 55 per cent of the total evacuation cost, but did not include invoices, contracts or the names of the operators.

Mr Aboagye further claimed that information available to the NPP indicated that the first three chartered flights were operated by Ethiopian Airlines and arranged through a person identified as Mr Vanderpuye.

He alleged that each flight may have been billed at nearly $300,000 above its actual cost, insisting that the original invoices would help clarify the discrepancy.

According to him, the Minister's documents put the cost of each flight at "$750,000, while the party's industry checks suggested that chartering a flight through Ethiopian Airlines or Air Tanzania should cost between $180,000 and $300,000."

The three flights, he said reportedly transported about 900 passengers from South Africa to Ghana.

“We put this to the Minister directly, and we invite him to prove it wrong with paper, not words. Publish the original Ethiopian Airlines invoices for all three flights, so we can have some proper conversation with the airline as to how and why it ripped off the country at such a crucial time,” he said.

Mr Aboagye also questioned the Ministry's relationship with Mr Vanderpuye, who he alleged arranged the flights.

He asked whether the Ministry's Chief Director had requested fresh invoices from Mr Vanderpuye in September and, if so, why invoices for flights completed months earlier needed to be reissued.

He further demanded the release of detailed records from Ghana's High Commission in Pretoria covering the flights, payments and assistance provided to the evacuees.

Mr Aboagye also called on Mr Ablakwa to "clarify allegations that his bodyguard had received $10,000 from the evacuation arrangements."

He asked the Minister to confirm whether the officer had been dismissed and explain the purpose of the alleged payment and the circumstances surrounding the reported dismissal.

“If the figures are honest, the original invoices will settle this in a day. If they are not produced, Ghanaians will draw their own conclusions,” he said.

The allegations of overbilling and the alleged payment to the bodyguard were not independently established in the statement. The Foreign Affairs Minister's response to the specific claims was not included in the material provided.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
