World.title: Asia Chip Selloff Tests Latin America Metals
World.content:
File photo: Shinjuku, Tokyo. Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 4.90% on the same day as the KOSPI.

SOUTH KOREA · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening South Korea’s KOSPI index fell 7.57% to 5,554.22 on 15 October 2026, its seventh straight loss, and Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 4.90%.

— Why it matters A lasting slump in Asian chip demand could cut Chinese industrial buying of Latin American copper, iron ore and other exports, weakening currencies and earnings.

— The numbers Samsung Electronics fell 9.48% and SK hynix 11.06%, while Korea’s September chip exports hit a record US$60.5 billion, up 260.3% from a year earlier.

— Who is who The KOSPI is South Korea’s main stock index; Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are its best-known memory-chip makers; the Nikkei 225 is Japan’s main index.

— What to watch China’s third-quarter GDP on 19 October, the Bank of Korea rate decision on 22 October and the US Federal Reserve decision on 28 October.

— Prediction markets Polymarket traders put the chance of a new KOSPI record high before 2028 at 27.5% (US$40,463 traded; 5:25 p.m. ET, 18 October 2026).

— What it means for you US investors in Brazilian, Chilean or Peruvian assets should check whether currency moves are eroding local share-price gains, especially in copper and mining equities.

A chip-led rout in Seoul and Tokyo on 15 October 2026 raised a question for Latin America: is it a one-day valuation shock or an early sign of weaker Asian demand for metals? One trading day cannot settle that, and the first signals from Latin American markets were mixed.

South Korea’s KOSPI index fell 7.57% on Thursday 15 October, led by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix. This analysis explains how a chip shock in Seoul can reach copper mines in Chile and iron ore ports in Brazil, and what US investors should watch, building on our Asia Intelligence Brief.

What Triggered the Selloff

The KOSPI ended at 5,554.22 after dipping as low as 5,450.81, its seventh straight daily loss and the longest losing streak since September 2024, the Korea JoongAng Daily reported. Sell-side trading curbs known as sidecars were triggered on both the KOSPI and the smaller KOSDAQ in the morning.

Latin America Power Index · October 2026 edition Brazil ranks 1st of 14 with 75.0 points. Strongest pillar: military means (100); weakest: state capacity & security (56). Alignment group: Hedging. WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

The exchange then halted trading on the main board for 20 minutes at 12:38 p.m. local time, after the index fell more than 8% from the previous close. Foreign investors sold a net 3.62 trillion won (about US$2.7 billion) of shares.

Three worries came together, according to the same report: a possible supply glut from Chinese chipmakers, doubts about returns on artificial-intelligence spending and the prospect of another US interest-rate rise. US consumer prices rose 3.7% in the year to September, up from 3.4% in August, the US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported on 14 October.

Samsung Electronics fell 9.48% to 210,000 won, and SK hynix fell 11.06% to about 1.26 million won. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped 4.90% to 64,425.95 the same day, according to RT market data.

Both indices recovered part of the losses on 16 October. The KOSPI rose 2.05% to 5,668.05 and the Nikkei 225 gained 1.39% to 65,324.29, but one day of recovery does not show that the selling has ended.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on US investors Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

The Transmission Chain to Latin America

A technology rout triggered by inflation worries generally pushes investors toward cash and US Treasury assets. The resulting dollar strength tends to weaken the Brazilian real, Chilean peso and Peruvian sol.

That creates mixed effects for Latin American economies. Exporters earn more local currency per dollar of sales, but dollar debt becomes dearer and foreign investors demand a larger risk premium.

For US investors, the first impact often shows in dollar returns rather than share prices. A Chilean copper producer can outperform in pesos and still produce a negative return for an unhedged US investor if the peso falls sharply.

What Latin American Markets Did on the Day

On 15 October the Brazilian real weakened 1.4% to 5.0970 per US dollar from 5.0278, RT data show. The Chilean peso moved the other way, firming 0.4% to 981.2 per dollar, while the Peruvian sol was almost flat at 3.438.

Chile is the most copper-exposed of the three, so that pattern does not look like a simple copper scare. It suggests investors treated Thursday mainly as an Asian technology event, not yet as a metals event.

The US-listed copper fund CPER slipped 0.53% to US$39.45 on 15 October and edged up to US$39.50 on 16 October. By 16 October the real stood at 5.0627, the peso at 984.83 and the sol at 3.4397 per dollar.

The China Channel

South Korea and Japan use large volumes of industrial commodities, but China is the pivotal buyer for Latin America. A Korean chip shock becomes a China-demand concern only if investors read it as a sign that the wider electronics or investment cycle is turning down.

Current orders do not yet show such a turn. Korea’s final September figures, released by the Korea Customs Service on 15 October, put chip exports at a record US$60.503 billion, up 260.3% from a year earlier.

Total exports reached a record US$121.1 billion, up 83.7%, and shipments to China rose 123.1% to US$26.06 billion, according to Chosun Biz. The selloff therefore reflects doubts about the price of future profits more than weak demand today.

Which Commodities React First

Copper is the cleanest barometer of Asian industrial demand. It combines deep financial liquidity with direct exposure to electrical equipment, manufacturing and construction.

A sustained break in copper alongside weaker Chinese purchasing data would suggest a real industrial slowdown rather than a repricing of Korean technology shares. Chile and Peru are directly exposed through export prices, mining profits and fiscal revenue.

Lithium needs more caution, because its prices can fall even when other industrial commodities rise. Mine expansions, inventories and changes in battery chemistry all play a part.

Iron ore is a China-property trade first. A one-day technology rout should not automatically be read as a Brazilian iron-ore shock, but the warning grows if iron ore, Chinese steel margins and the yuan weaken together.

Soybeans and oil are second-round exposures. They respond less to memory-chip demand than to the income and currency effects of a broader Asian slowdown.

For context on the metal, see our guide to copper in Latin America and the copper market report for 15 October. The guide covers mines, prices and politics.

Country Effects and US Investor Exposure

Brazil combines large exposure to iron ore, soybeans and oil with a liquid equity market widely owned by global investors. Lower iron ore prices would reduce Vale’s earnings, while weaker soy prices would pressure farm margins.

The Brazilian market could still outperform if the selloff stays concentrated in Asian technology shares and investors rotate toward value or dividend stocks. The key question is whether Brazil is treated as a commodity beneficiary or as a high-beta emerging market.

Chile is the most direct Latin American equity and currency proxy for a copper-centred Asian slowdown. Lower copper prices reduce mining cash flow and tax receipts, while a weaker peso erodes dollar returns for foreign investors.

Peru is exposed through copper, gold and other minerals, and its currency and equities are sensitive to foreign portfolio flows. Gold offers a partial counterweight in broader financial stress, but a stronger dollar and higher US rates can limit that protection.

US investors should separate three risks: equity risk from falling share prices, commodity risk from lower Asian demand and currency risk from a weaker real, peso or sol. Hedged exchange-traded products or companies with large dollar revenues can reduce, but not remove, currency exposure.

File photo: an open-pit copper mine in northern Chile.

What Would Make This a Commodity Shock

The cause and duration of a technology selloff matter more than its one-day percentage decline. A short valuation reset can leave commodity demand intact, while a prolonged retreat with falling Chinese output and credit growth can become an emerging-market export shock.

The central conclusion is that a South Korean chip-led rout does not automatically mean a Latin American commodity crash. It becomes consequential when markets read it as evidence of weaker Chinese manufacturing, slower global investment and tighter US financial conditions.

What Prediction Markets Say

Implied probabilities as of 5:25 p.m. ET, 18 October 2026 — KOSPI record high Polymarket, “KOSPI all-time high before 2028?”: 27.5% , US$40,463 traded.

— Fed rate hike in 2026 Polymarket, “Another Fed rate hike in 2026?”: 78.5% , US$864,159 traded.

— Next Fed hike Kalshi, “Next Fed rate hike?”: 81% before 2027. Kalshi is regulated in the US by the CFTC.

These prices are bets, not polls, and we do not have their price history around 15 October. They show that traders still see a US rate rise as likely, which is the pressure that hit Asian chip shares.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for You

If you hold Brazilian, Chilean or Peruvian equities, check whether currency losses are eroding local share-price gains. A Chilean copper producer can rise in pesos and still lose value in dollars.

If you are weighing new positions, copper miners offer the most direct exposure to the Asia demand story but also the most concentrated China risk. Diversified Brazilian exporters may give more cushion if the selloff stays confined to technology shares.

What Is Not Known

It is not yet known whether the selloff reflects a real slowdown in Asian industrial demand or a repricing of expensive technology shares. Korea’s September export data still show exceptional strength.

Spot prices for copper, iron ore and lithium are outside this analysis, so the commodity read-through rests on currency moves and the copper fund. The direction of US interest rates is also unsettled until the Federal Reserve meets.

What to Watch

The most convincing sign of contagion would be Asian tech shares down, copper down, China data weaker, the dollar up and Latin American currencies falling together. Any single signal can be noise.

China publishes third-quarter GDP and September industrial output at 02:00 UTC on Monday 19 October (10:00 p.m. ET on Sunday). The RT calendar shows a forecast of 4.4% year-on-year growth against 4.3% before, and industrial output of 5.4% against 5.2%.

The Bank of Korea decides on rates at 01:00 UTC on 22 October, with the previous level at 3.00%. The US Federal Reserve announces its decision at 18:00 UTC (2 p.m. ET) on 28 October.

Korea’s next monthly trade release will show whether the chip boom continued into October. For background on the trading halts, see our explainer on how KOSPI circuit breakers work; our Asia coverage follows the region.

Frequently Asked Questions

How does an Asian tech selloff affect Latin American commodity exporters?

An Asian technology rout can reduce Chinese industrial demand for copper, iron ore and other Latin American exports. It also tends to strengthen the US dollar, which weakens Latin American currencies and can erode dollar returns for foreign investors.

Which Latin American countries are most exposed to a Korean chip selloff?

Chile is the most direct proxy for copper-centred Asian demand, followed by Peru. Brazil has broader exposure through iron ore, soybeans and oil, and its mix of commodities can give some cushion.

What happened to South Korean markets on 15 October 2026?

The KOSPI fell 7.57% to 5,554.22, its seventh straight loss, and trading was halted for 20 minutes. Samsung Electronics fell 9.48%, SK hynix fell 11.06% and Japan’s Nikkei 225 fell 4.90%.

Is a technology selloff the same as a commodity crash?

Not by itself: a short valuation reset can leave commodity demand intact. It becomes a commodity shock only if markets read it as a sign of weaker Chinese manufacturing and slower global investment.

Did Latin American currencies fall on 15 October?

Not uniformly. The Brazilian real weakened 1.4% against the US dollar, the Chilean peso firmed 0.4% and the Peruvian sol was almost unchanged, according to RT data.

How can US investors limit currency risk in Latin America?

Hedged exchange-traded products or companies with large dollar revenues can reduce currency exposure. Investors should also check whether local share-price gains are being eroded by a weaker real, peso or sol.

World.title: EU Weighs Windfall Tax on Energy Profits
World.content:
File photo: the ENAP Aconcagua oil refinery in Concón, Chile.

EUROPEAN UNION · ANALYSIS

Key Facts — What is happening Six EU governments asked for an EU-level discussion of a new tax on oil and gas windfall profits, and on 9 October 2026 finance ministers asked the Commission to explore it, with any measures national in scope.

— Why it matters A new levy could cut after-tax returns on European energy sales and trigger contract talks for US and Latin American LNG and crude exporters.

— The numbers The 2022 EU levy had a minimum rate of 33% and collected €26.15 billion (US$29.4 billion) over tax years 2022 and 2023.

— Who is who Austria, Germany, Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain asked for the discussion; Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis says member states are better placed to set such taxes.

— What to watch Whether the working group produces a formal proposal, and whether Poland-style national levies spread before any EU-wide rule.

— What it means for you US energy firms with EU subsidiaries, permanent establishments or flexible LNG contracts could face higher tax exposure if a new levy follows the 2022 model.

Six EU governments want Brussels to study a new tax on oil and gas profits, but no decision on one was reported from the 15–16 October summit. For US and Latin American exporters, the design of any levy matters more than the headline.

Energy prices in Europe have jumped since the war in Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Italian outlet Eunews. On 9 October 2026, finance ministers meeting in Luxembourg asked the European Commission to explore taxing the windfall profits of oil and gas companies.

This analysis explains the 2022 precedent, who is pushing for a new levy and what it could mean for suppliers in the United States and Latin America. It draws on the Europe Intelligence Brief of 15 October 2026 and on EU documents.

What Happened in October

Austria, Germany, Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain launched a joint initiative asking for an EU-level discussion of extra taxes on oil and gas windfall profits. Finance ministers took it up at the Economic and Financial Affairs Council, known as Ecofin, on 9 October 2026.

Ireland’s finance minister Simon Harris, who chaired the meeting, said the Commission had been given a mandate to explore the possibility of such taxes. KPMG reported him adding that any legislative proposal remains a matter for the Commission.

According to KPMG’s EU tax newsletter, ministers also agreed to a Commission-led working group to look at options and share best practice. Eunews reported that any measures would be national in scope, with Commission technical and legal support, and no date was given for any proposal.

Dombrovskis, the commissioner for the economy, said the Commission believes member states are better placed to set taxes in this area. In practice, Brussels is open to studying a levy but has not endorsed an EU-wide one.

EU leaders then met in Brussels on 15 and 16 October. Belga reported that they asked the Commission to look again at the planned carbon charge on transport and heating, and we found no report of a windfall-tax decision from the summit.

How the 2022 Windfall Tax Worked

The European Union already has a template for taxing energy windfalls. Council Regulation (EU) 2022/1854, adopted on 6 October 2022, created a temporary solidarity contribution on fossil-fuel companies.

The measure applied to EU companies and permanent establishments whose relevant activities represented at least 75% of turnover. Covered sectors included crude petroleum extraction, natural gas, coal and refining.

The tax base was taxable profit exceeding by more than 20% the average taxable profits for the four fiscal years beginning on or after 1 January 2018. Only the portion above that baseline was subject to the levy.

The EU required a minimum rate of 33% on that excess-profit base for 2022 and/or 2023. Member states could impose higher rates.

The Commission’s final report, published on 15 May 2025, says the contribution collected €26.15 billion (US$29.4 billion) across tax years 2022 and 2023. Counting estimated remaining 2023 proceeds, the total would reach €28.66 billion (US$32.2 billion).

Member states mostly used the money for support measures for energy consumers, especially vulnerable households. Euro conversions use the EUR/USD rate of 1.1237 on 16 October 2026 (RT).

Who Backs a New Levy, and Who Hesitates

The six governments behind the joint initiative asked for an EU-level discussion of extra taxes on oil and gas windfall profits. The Commission is more cautious and stresses that national governments decide on taxes.

Poland has already acted on its own. President Karol Nawrocki signed a law on 1 October 2026 that charges 60% of excess profits from liquid fuel sales, measured against each company’s 2025 average margin plus 20%.

The Polish government expects about PLN 4 billion (about US$1.0 billion) from the levy. It offsets part of the cost of cutting fuel taxes for consumers, according to Notes from Poland.

The legal route will shape the outcome. The 2022 contribution was adopted as an emergency measure under Article 122 of the EU treaty, while an ordinary tax law would normally need every member state to agree.

The Numbers That Matter

The 2022 framework offers the clearest guide to what a new measure could look like. These are the figures that defined the original levy.

33% minimum rate on surplus profits, with member states free to go higher.

The 2022 approach targeted taxable profits, not every barrel of oil or cubic metre of gas sold. A company with high revenue but normal margins would not necessarily face the same burden as one whose profits sharply exceeded its historical baseline.

What a New Levy Could Cover

A future measure could resemble the 2022 model, but its scope is not settled. The most plausible elements include a temporary tax, a focus on oil and gas companies, a historical profit baseline and a minimum EU-wide rate with national implementation.

It could also be narrower or broader than in 2022. It might target EU-based producers and refiners, permanent establishments, trading profits booked in EU jurisdictions, or companies that sell LNG, crude or refined products to European buyers.

The last category would be legally and commercially sensitive. The 2022 regulation focused on EU companies and permanent establishments in specified upstream and refining activities, not on every foreign supplier whose cargo entered the EU.

Effects on Supply Contracts and LNG Buyers

A windfall tax would not automatically invalidate existing supply contracts. The practical question is who bears the economic cost.

Long-term LNG and oil contracts usually allocate price, tax and change-in-law risks through detailed clauses. A new levy could trigger disputes over whether it is a seller cost and whether destination-country taxes can be added to the price.

For European buyers, the immediate effect would depend on whether the tax falls on the supplier, the intermediary or the buyer. A levy on a producer’s profits may not appear as a separate line item, but the supplier may seek higher prices at renewal.

The US and Latin American Angles

US energy companies could be affected in three main ways. First, a US oil, gas or refining group with European operations could face the levy if the final rules follow the 2022 model and cover qualifying EU entities or permanent establishments.

Second, US LNG exporters selling into Europe could face pressure from buyers seeking to pass through or renegotiate any new tax-related cost. Third, if the levy lowers after-tax returns on European sales, exporters could place more cargoes in Asia when destination clauses allow.

For Latin American exporters, the most exposed companies would likely be those with EU subsidiaries, European refining or trading businesses, or profits booked through EU entities. Exporters selling crude or LNG directly from Latin America to Europe would not necessarily be taxed on their global production profits under a 2022-style model.

Exposure would rise if the EU designed the measure around sales into the EU rather than profits of EU-based entities. That distinction is the single most important variable for foreign suppliers.

Readers following the supply side can find more in our reports on Europe’s winter gas risk and the LNG rivalry and on Petrobras locking in US LNG for two decades. Our Europe coverage tracks the Brussels debate.

File photo: a tanker passes an offshore wind farm.

The Scenarios

The scenario closest to what Ecofin described is national levies with EU coordination, as in Poland. That patchwork could complicate contracting and encourage companies to compare EU jurisdictions.

A second scenario is a narrow, temporary EU levy modelled on the 2022 framework. It would apply to EU-based producers and refiners, use a historical profit baseline and leave foreign exporters without EU establishments largely untouched.

A more disruptive scenario is a broader measure that targets sales into the EU or trading profits booked in EU jurisdictions. That could affect US and Latin American suppliers directly and push flexible cargoes toward Asia.

What It Means for You

If you hold shares in US or Latin American energy companies with European operations, check whether those operations are EU subsidiaries or permanent establishments. Those are the entities most likely to fall within a 2022-style levy.

If you manage LNG or crude supply contracts with European buyers, review the change-in-law and tax pass-through clauses now. The time to clarify who bears a new tax is before it is enacted.

If you follow policy, watch whether the working group produces a formal proposal or only a technical assessment. The difference decides whether the idea reaches the Council with legal force.

What Is Not Known

The tax base is not known. It could be accounting profit, taxable profit, market revenue or a mix, and each would affect suppliers and buyers differently.

The territorial scope, rate and duration are not known. The 2022 minimum was 33% and member states could go higher, while the new measure could last one year, two or longer.

The timetable and legal instrument are not known. No date was given, and a regulation would apply directly while a directive would need national laws.

What to Watch

The Commission-led working group is the next concrete step. Its assessment will show whether a formal proposal follows.

National measures are moving on their own timelines, with Poland’s law already signed. More governments may copy it before Brussels decides.

The calendar offers two markers for energy costs. The European Central Bank announces its rate decision on 29 October, and the euro-area inflation estimate for October is due on 4 November (RT calendar).

Frequently Asked Questions

What is an EU windfall tax on energy companies?

An EU windfall tax is a temporary levy on profits considered unusually high because of external events such as war or supply disruption. The 2022 version applied a minimum 33% rate to taxable profits above a four-year average plus 20%.

Which countries want a new EU windfall tax?

Austria, Germany, Italy, Poland, Portugal and Spain launched a joint initiative asking for an EU-level discussion. Finance ministers took it up on 9 October 2026 and agreed to a Commission-led working group.

Will a new EU windfall tax apply to US LNG exporters?

US LNG exporters would not automatically become liable merely because they sell energy to Europe. Exposure would depend on whether a measure covers EU subsidiaries, permanent establishments or sales into the EU.

Could a windfall tax affect existing LNG supply contracts?

A windfall tax would not automatically invalidate existing contracts, but it could trigger disputes over change-in-law clauses and tax pass-through. The practical question is who bears the economic cost.

What is the difference between the 2022 tax and the 2026 discussion?

The 2022 measure was a temporary solidarity contribution adopted as a Council regulation. The 2026 discussion is still at the examination stage, with no Commission proposal and no timetable.

World.title: Senegal Jeweler Found Dead in Zac Mbao Shop
World.content:
Crime: Senegal

Key Facts —Who. Mouhamadou Khabane Guèye, a 55-year-old jeweller originally from Mbacké. —What. Found dead in his jewellery shop; the cause of death awaits a forensic examination, and local outlets differ on what was taken. —Where. Zac Mbao, Rufisque area, Dakar region, Senegal. —When. Saturday 17 October 2026, in the evening; Seneweb says police were alerted at about 9:28 pm. —As of 18 October 2026, 21:00 GMT. No arrests reported.

A jeweller was found dead in his shop in Zac Mbao, in the Rufisque area of Senegal’s Dakar region, on the evening of Saturday 17 October 2026. Local outlets differ on the cause of death and on what was taken, and no arrests had been reported by the evening of 18 October.

What We Know

Americans who travel to Dakar or trade in jewellery and gold will want to understand this case, because it concerns the security of a working shop in the Rufisque area. Readers planning a trip should check current official travel advice, including guidance from the US State Department.

The victim was Mouhamadou Khabane Guèye, a jeweller who is also named Modou Khabane Gueye or Mouhamed Khabane Guèye in local reports. Seneweb describes him as 55 years old and originally from Mbacké.

Aerial view of Dakar. (File photo)

Dakarposte says he left a wife and three children, two daughters and a son. We relay that detail as reported by Dakarposte, and we extend our condolences to his family.

His body was found in his jewellery shop in Zac Mbao on Saturday 17 October 2026. Seneweb says police were alerted at about 9:28 pm, and that he lay behind the counter.

Seneweb reports that police found a deep wound on the left side of the head. It also lists bruises on the left forearm and the right thigh, which Seneweb links to a violent struggle.

The same report mentions blood traces on the walls and says the electrical breaker had been cut. Surveillance cameras had been removed, but police recovered the central recording unit.

Officers from the Rufisque Central Police Station and the technical and scientific police attended the scene. Seneweb names Cheikh Diakhoumpa as the prosecutor of the Rufisque court.

Local outlets differ on the cause of death and on what was taken. Dakarposte reports that armed robbers took a large quantity of gold and cash, and SENTV says they took the shop’s entire gold stock.

SENTV adds that the assailants allegedly slit the victim’s throat, a detail the other two outlets do not carry. Seneweb, by contrast, says the safe showed signs of attempted forced entry but stayed closed.

Dakarposte says the cause of death awaits a forensic examination. Neither Dakarposte nor SENTV quotes a police or prosecutor statement in the articles we reviewed.

What Is Not Known

The cause of death has not been confirmed, and no forensic result has been reported. It is also unclear whether the account of an armed robbery or the account of a closed safe is accurate.

The quantity of gold and cash said to be missing has not been confirmed by police or the prosecutor. The reports we reviewed do not mention an official inventory of the shop.

No arrests were reported as of the evening of 18 October 2026. The motive, the number of people involved and the identity of anyone responsible are all unknown.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

For travellers, this is a single criminal investigation, and the reports do not describe any wider threat to visitors. Official travel advice remains the best guide to current conditions in the Dakar region.

Businesses in the jewellery and gold trade will note the reported details, including the cut electrical breaker and the removed cameras. Those details come from one outlet, and none of the reports quotes a police conclusion.

US readers with business ties in Dakar should treat early local reports with care. The accounts differ on basic points, and we attribute each version to the outlet that published it.

Our Senegal coverage follows developments in the country. We have not independently verified the local accounts above.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was the man found dead in Zac Mbao?

He was Mouhamadou Khabane Guèye, a jeweller whom Seneweb describes as 55 years old and originally from Mbacké. Dakarposte says he had a wife and three children.

Where and when was he found?

He was found in his jewellery shop in Zac Mbao, in the Rufisque area of the Dakar region, on Saturday 17 October 2026. Seneweb says police were alerted at about 9:28 pm.

Have there been any arrests?

No arrests had been reported as of the evening of 18 October 2026. Dakarposte and SENTV quote no police or prosecutor statement in the articles we reviewed.

What should US travellers do?

This is a single criminal case, and the reports describe no wider threat to visitors. Travellers should check current official travel advice before planning a trip to Senegal.

Sources Seneweb · Dakarposte · SENTV

World.title: At Least 10 Die in West Darfur Drone Strike
World.content:
Breaking: Sudan

A drone strike killed at least 10 civilians on Saturday, 17 October 2026, in Sanaqit, West Darfur, Sudan, near the Chadian border. The attack is blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF), whose representatives could not be reached for comment.

For US readers, the strike matters because the Chad border region shelters displaced families and is where aid groups work. It also bears on the debate over sanctions, humanitarian funding and pressure on the warring sides.

Key Facts —Who. At least 10 civilians were killed and 5 wounded. The paramilitary RSF is blamed for the attack. —What. A drone strike hit displaced people harvesting crops. A second report counts 11 dead, including 9 children. —Where. Sanaqit, in Bir Siliba, Sirba locality, West Darfur, Sudan. The area lies near the border with Chad. —When. Saturday, 17 October 2026. Reports emerged on 18 October 2026. —Prediction markets. Polymarket prices a Sudan civil war ceasefire by 31 December 2026 at 11.0%. About US$119,600 has been traded, as of 18 October 2026, about 15:11 ET. —As of. 18 October 2026, 19:20 GMT. Figures may change as reports are confirmed.

What We Know

Radio Tamazuj reported on 18 October 2026 that at least 10 civilians died and 5 were wounded. The strike hit Sanaqit, also spelled Sanakit or Hajar Sanakit, in the Bir Siliba administrative unit of Sirba locality.

Babiker Hamdein, health minister of the Darfur regional government, reported the dead and wounded. Sudan Horizon spells his surname Hamdine.

Hamdein said the victims were displaced people from the villages of Naroma, Karmalia and Qarmba. Reports spell these names differently, including Narouma and Qaqrumba.

The villagers fled after their homes were burned and looted. They had sought refuge near the Chadian border.

Leaders of the Mararit tribe said the victims were harvesting crops when the drone struck. Those hit included children as young as three and older people.

Sudan Horizon, citing the social welfare ministry of the Darfur regional government, reported 11 dead, including nine children. The figures differ, so we say at least 10 until a fuller count emerges.

Major Mutawakkil Ali Wakil, spokesman for the Joint Force, condemned the attack. The Joint Force is a group of armed factions allied with the army.

He said: “Targeting innocent civilians constitutes a grave violation of international humanitarian law.” He also demanded accountability.

Hamdein called the attack a grave violation of international humanitarian law and urged international responsibility. According to Sudan Horizon, he also asked that the RSF be designated a terrorist organisation.

Sudan has been at war since April 2023, with the army (SAF) fighting the RSF. Both sides have used drones in attacks.

Our earlier reports include an RSF drone strike on a courthouse in North Kordofan and an earlier Blue Nile drone strike, which killed at least 30 people. More is in our report on how a UN panel links Colombian contractors to Sudan’s war and our Africa section.

File photo: health workers in Sudan’s Blue Nile state. Not from the area of the strike.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

What Is Not Known

The final death toll is unconfirmed. Reports give 10 and 11 dead, and only one report gives a number of wounded.

The RSF has not responded to the allegation. The reports we reviewed do not state the type of drone or where it was launched.

It is unclear whether any international body will act on the calls for accountability. So far those calls, including the terrorist designation request, exist only as statements.

Nothing in the reports explains why this village was targeted. We do not speculate on motive or on who carried out the strike beyond the attribution to the RSF.

What Prediction Markets Say

Polymarket’s contract “Sudan civil war ceasefire by December 31, 2026” trades at 11.0%, an implied probability. About US$119,600 has been traded, as of 18 October 2026, about 15:11 ET.

These prices are bets by traders, not polls. They reflect a view on a ceasefire by year-end and say nothing about who carried out this strike.

Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What It Means for Travelers and US Readers

Darfur and the border region with Chad remain extremely dangerous for travellers and aid workers. The victims were hit while harvesting crops, which shows how ordinary daily work carries risk.

Because drones are now a common weapon in this war, similar reports may continue. Early death tolls from remote areas should be treated as provisional.

Readers following US sanctions, aid or refugee policy should watch for a confirmed toll and any response from the RSF. A clearer attribution would shape those debates.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happened in West Darfur on 17 October 2026?

A drone strike hit Sanaqit in Sirba locality, near the Chadian border, on Saturday, 17 October 2026. At least 10 civilians were killed and 5 wounded, according to Radio Tamazuj.

Who is blamed for the attack?

The paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) are blamed. RSF representatives could not be reached for comment, so the attribution remains an allegation.

How many people died?

Radio Tamazuj reports at least 10 dead, while Sudan Horizon reports 11, including nine children. The figures differ, so we use at least 10.

Why does this matter to US readers?

The area near Chad shelters displaced people and is a place where aid groups work. The strike also feeds the debate over sanctions and humanitarian funding.

World.title: Lua Blanco of Rebelde Brasil Dies at 39
World.content:
Lua Blanco, the Brazilian actress and singer known as Roberta Messi in Rebelde Brasil, has died at the age of 39. Her brother Daniel Blanco announced the death on Instagram on Sunday, 18 October 2026.

Rebelde is a franchise that many readers in the United States know through the original Rebelde and the band RBD. The Brazilian version aired on Record from 2011 to 2012, and Blanco was one of its cast members.

This report covers the news from Brazil and draws on Portuguese-language reports. We separate what the family and the press have confirmed from what is still unknown.

Key Facts —Who. Lua Blanco, Brazilian actress and singer, known as Roberta Messi in Rebelde Brasil. —What. She died aged 39; her brother Daniel Blanco announced it on Instagram. —Where. Brazil. She was born in São Paulo, and the place of death has not been reported. —When. Sunday, 18 October 2026; a farewell is reported for Monday, 19 October 2026. —Status. As of 18 October 2026, 19:00 GMT

Prediction markets · who wins the runoff Implied chance of winning Brazil’s presidency on 25 October, from traders’ prices. Polymarket Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21.5% (US$187 million traded) Kalshi (regulated in the US by the CFTC) Flávio Bolsonaro 79% · Lula 21% As of 18 October, 6:40 pm ET (23:40 Lisbon), updated every 20 minutes. Prices are bets, not polls, and can move fast. Why we show this: prediction markets turn real-money bets into a live probability that moves within minutes of the news, which is why investors, campaigns and newsrooms in the United States now follow them closely. We show them next to polls and official results, never instead of them.

What We Know

Blanco was born on 5 March 1987 in São Paulo and died on Sunday, 18 October 2026, aged 39. Her brother Daniel Blanco shared the news on Instagram.

He wrote that she died in peace, surrounded by the love of family and friends and sustained by her faith. He also wrote that she had fought cancer in recent months.

He did not name the type of cancer. We will not speculate about her illness.

WatchRating below investment grade (BB); public debt at 93% of GDP. See the full index, the business lens and the data →

This report draws on Terra, Metrópoles and O Tempo, three Brazilian outlets publishing in Portuguese. O Tempo also reported her death at 39.

Her sister Anaterra Blanco paid tribute in her Instagram Stories, writing in Portuguese. She called life “um sopro” (a breath), told her sister “te amo” (I love you) and wrote that she lives on in them forever.

Blanco was best known as Roberta Messi in Rebelde Brasil, shown on Record in 2011 and 2012. She was also a member of Rebeldes, the band that grew out of the series with five other cast members.

Before Rebelde Brasil, she was the singer and songwriter of the band Lágrima Flor. She was also the granddaughter of the composer and bossa nova musician Billy Blanco.

Bossa nova is the Brazilian style that blends samba with jazz. Billy Blanco worked in that tradition.

Record is a Brazilian television network. It aired both Rebelde Brasil and, in 2013, Pecado Mortal.

O Tempo lists other roles, including Três Irmãs in 2008, Malhação in 2009 and Pecado Mortal in 2013 on Record.

Metrópoles reports that a farewell will be held on Monday, 19 October 2026, from 13:00 to 16:00 local time. Rio de Janeiro is three hours behind GMT, so that is 16:00 to 19:00 GMT, and the venue is chapel 06 at the Cemitério Vertical Memorial do Carmo in Rio de Janeiro.

On the US East Coast, that farewell window runs from 12:00 to 15:00 on Monday, Eastern Daylight Time. The United States stays on daylight time until 1 November 2026.

Terra reports that the family has asked for privacy in its grief. The farewell schedule is Metrópoles’s account, and it may change.

What Is Not Known

The reports we reviewed do not say where Blanco died. They also do not name the type of cancer.

Details of a burial beyond Monday’s farewell have not been reported. The family has asked for privacy, and we will not press for more.

We have not seen confirmation of whether the farewell is open to the public. We have also not seen a statement from Record.

We have no verified account of her final months beyond her brother’s message. If the family shares more, we will update this article in full.

What It Means for Readers Outside Brazil

Rebelde began as a Mexican telenovela, and its cast formed the band RBD. The format later travelled to other countries, including Brazil.

Malhação, one of her earlier roles, is a long-running Brazilian youth drama. It shows that her screen career began before Rebelde Brasil.

Brazil’s version, broadcast by Record from 2011 to 2012, produced its own band, Rebeldes. Blanco was among its members.

Readers who know the franchise through RBD will recognise the outline of her career. We have no information on whether the Brazilian version aired outside Brazil.

For now, the main public statements come from her brother and sister on Instagram. The Portuguese-language reports linked below carry the details.

Frequently Asked Questions

Who was Lua Blanco?

Lua Blanco was a Brazilian actress and singer, born on 5 March 1987 in São Paulo. She was best known as Roberta Messi in Rebelde Brasil.

When did Lua Blanco die?

She died on Sunday, 18 October 2026, aged 39, according to her brother Daniel Blanco. He wrote that she had fought cancer in recent months, but did not name the type.

What was Lua Blanco known for?

She played Roberta Messi in Rebelde Brasil on Record from 2011 to 2012. She was also a member of the band Rebeldes and earlier sang in the band Lágrima Flor.

When is the farewell for Lua Blanco?

Metrópoles reports a farewell on Monday, 19 October 2026, from 13:00 to 16:00 local time. It is reported for chapel 06 at the Cemitério Vertical Memorial do Carmo in Rio de Janeiro.

BRAZIL · ELECTIONS

Published Sunday, 18 October, 2:16 p.m. ET · Source: Folha de S.Paulo, Brazil’s electoral court (TSE)

Key Facts The country Brazil, Latin America’s largest country, elects its president in a runoff on Sunday 25 October between President Lula and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro.

What changed On Sunday 18 October the electoral court (TSE) updated its data to show 2,033 voting sections with a new address for the runoff.

The numbers About 592,000 voters are affected, and 21.08% of the electorate stayed away in the first round on 4 October.

The request Lula’s coalition asked the court on Sunday to publicise the moves widely and to help voters travel.

Power Index Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in Brazil ranks 1st of 14 in The Rio Times Latin America Power Index , with 75.0 points (October 2026 edition).

Prediction markets Polymarket gives Flávio Bolsonaro an 80.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff (18 October, 2:16 p.m. ET). Polymarket puts Flávio Bolsonaro’s chance of winning at 79% and Kalshi at 80% (Lula: 21% and 20% ), as of 18 October, 5:40 pm ET ; prices are bets, not polls.

Still open The sources do not explain why this count of 2,033 sections differs from the 4,352 reported as of Friday.

Brazil’s electoral court (TSE) changed the voting address of 2,033 sections for the 25 October runoff, affecting about 592,000 voters, according to data it updated on Sunday 18 October. Folha de S.Paulo reported the figures at 11:27 a.m. ET.

The coalition of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, asked the court the same day to publicise the moves widely before the Brazil election 2026 runoff against Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro. A section is a polling station with its own voter list, and the Brazil runoff date is Sunday 25 October.

What the Electoral Court Changed

The TSE moved 2,033 sections to new buildings between the first round and the runoff, Folha reported. The court said voters can check their address in its Electoral Self-Service portal or in the e-Título app, its voter-ID app.

O Tempo also reported 592,000 affected voters. Voting is compulsory for most adults, so a wrong address can cost a vote.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, The LatAm Brief. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why the Addresses Moved

The court said the changes followed storms in some regions, damage to buildings and last-minute repairs, Folha reported. It added that each local electoral zone decides, according to the buildings available, so the TSE does not order the moves centrally.

The TSE had reported a separate count of 4,352 sections as of Friday 16 October, Agência Brasil reported, and we covered it in Brazil Moves 4,352 Polling Sites for Runoff. The sources do not say how that figure relates to today’s 2,033.

What Lula’s Coalition Is Asking

Lula’s coalition, led by his Workers’ Party (PT), filed a request with the court on Sunday, Folha reported. It asked for wide publicity of the changes and for measures to help voters reach their new polling places.

The lawyers pointed to the 21.08% abstention in the first round and said many people could not vote because their polling place had moved. They argued that if the state makes voting compulsory, it must make sure voters know where to go, Folha reported.

O Antagonista also reported the request.

What It Means for US Readers

A runoff this close can turn on turnout, so a dispute over how well voters were told where to vote may become part of the post-election argument. Investors in Brazilian stocks, bonds and US-listed shares should expect turnout and process questions to feed the news on the night of 25 October.

For readers following the race from the United States, the practical point is that each Brazilian voter must go to the address now on file with the electoral court.

What Prediction Markets Say

On Polymarket, an online prediction market, bettors give Flávio Bolsonaro an 80.0% chance of winning the 25 October runoff and Lula 20.5% (18 October, 2:16 p.m. ET). The “Brazil Presidential Election” market has drawn about US$187.2 million in total bets.

What Is Not Known

It is not known whether the TSE will answer the coalition’s request or add publicity measures before 25 October. The court has not said how the 2,033 sections reported on Sunday relate to the 4,352 reported as of Friday.

It is also not known how many of the 592,000 voters will fail to find their new address, or whether that would change the result. Turnout depends on many other factors, including weather and the closeness of the race.

How many Brazilian voters have a new polling place for the runoff?

The TSE data updated on Sunday 18 October show 2,033 sections with a new address, affecting about 592,000 voters. The court announced a separate count of 4,352 sections on Friday 16 October.

How can voters check their polling place?

They can use the TSE Electoral Self-Service portal or the e-Título app, the electoral court’s voter-ID app. Both show the current address for the runoff.

Why did some polling places change?

The court cited storms, building damage and last-minute repairs in some regions. Each local electoral zone decides, so the TSE does not order the moves centrally.

Key Facts What happened A driver struck a 67-year-old man at a pro-Lula rally in Belo Horizonte on Saturday 17 October, at about 5:31 p.m. ET (6:31 p.m. Brasília time).

The arrest Police arrested the driver in flagrante on suspicion of attempted homicide, and he was taken to a Civil Police station.

A driver ran into a 67-year-old man during a pro-Lula demonstration in Belo Horizonte on Saturday 17 October, and police arrested him on suspicion of attempted homicide. The incident, which Folha de S.Paulo reported on Sunday, came a week before the Brazil election 2026 runoff.

Belo Horizonte is the capital of Minas Gerais, one of Brazil’s most populous states. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, Brazil’s president, faces Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, senator for Rio de Janeiro, in the 25 October vote.

What Police and Witnesses Report

The man was hit at about 6:31 p.m. Brasília time at the corner of Rua da Bahia and Rua Tupinambás in the city centre, Metrópoles reported. The driver of a yellow Volkswagen Up ran a red light, and a municipal guard saw it happen, according to CNN Brasil.

The victim was taken to the João XXIII emergency hospital. Metrópoles reported an ankle fracture, while O Tempo spoke of foot injuries, and Folha said his overall condition had not been disclosed.

World.title: Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border
World.content:
Help needed to recover bag with passport, US cash and visa left at Western Border

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A San Ignacio family is asking the public for help to recover a bag left behind at the Belize Western Border.

According to the family, a woman forgot her black Michael Kors tote bag on a bench outside the money exchange booth near the taxi stand on the night of Monday, October 12, while waiting for her ride.

The bag contained US cash, her passport with an American visa, a credit card and other personal belongings.

The family says video footage appears to show a woman in red shorts and a black blouse picking up the bag and getting into a red car.

They are asking anyone who can help identify the person or vehicle to come forward. A reward is being offered.

If you have information, please call or WhatsApp 610 8117.

World.title: 24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk
World.content:
24 live rounds and suspected cocaine found hidden under cement block in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): Orange Walk police have recovered live ammunition and suspected cocaine hidden in an empty lot in Orange Walk Town.

Police say that around 8:00pm on Friday, October 16, officers from the Orange Walk GI3 Unit acted on information that someone had hidden something in a bushy lot at the corner of Chips Alley and Cabbage Street.

During checks, an officer found a green plastic bag tucked under a cement block.

Inside were 24 live 9mm rounds, 13 Luger brand and 11 S&B brand, along with a small plastic bag of white powder suspected to be cocaine.

The suspected cocaine weighed 7.3 grams.

No one was in the area at the time, and both the ammunition and drugs were sealed and logged as found property.

World.title: Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk
World.content:
Teen reports being beaten with belt by stepfather in Orange Walk

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 13 year old boy from Orange Walk District has reported to police that he was struck with a belt by his stepfather.

The boy visited the Orange Walk Police Station on Friday, October 16, accompanied by his biological father.

He told police that earlier that afternoon, his stepfather became upset after seeing his younger sibling walking with some boys the teen knew from school. He said his stepfather then lashed him with a belt on his hand and lower back.

According to the report, the boy was then told to pack his belongings and leave to stay with relatives. He later made his way to his father’s home, and his father took him to the police station.

A medico legal form was issued. The boy has been placed in the care of his father, and both parents have been instructed to report to the Human Services Department on Monday, October 19, for a follow up.

World.title: ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise
World.content:
ATM Cave and Barton Creek closed as river levels rise

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): The Actun Tunichil Muknal (ATM) and Barton Creek Archaeological Reserves are closed to visitors today because of elevated river levels.

The Institute of Archaeology of the National Institute of Culture and History (IA/NICH) made the announcement early Sunday morning, October 18.

All water related tour activities have also been suspended at the Nohoch Che’en Archaeological Reserve, a popular cave tubing destination.

All other archaeological reserves remain open for visitors.

The IA/NICH says it is monitoring conditions and will provide updates as necessary.

The closures come after days of heavy rain across the country, with an excessive rainfall warning issued by the National Meteorological Service.

World.title: Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded
World.content:
Swerving Toyota stop ends with taxi driver arrested and car impounded

By Breaking Belize News Staff (HP): A 51 year old taxi driver of Savannah Street, Orange Walk Town, has been charged with failing to provide a specimen.

He is Jaime Gomez.

Police say officers on burglary patrol on San Antonio Road around 10:50pm on Thursday, October 15, saw a white Toyota Corolla swerving from side to side on Savannah Street.

When officers stopped the car, Gomez allegedly got out of the driver’s side staggering, leaving the engine running and headlights on. Officers say they smelled a strong odour of alcohol on his breath.

He was arrested for driving under the influence and taken to the Orange Walk Police Station, where he was asked for a urine specimen. Police say he refused three times.

He was then taken to the Northern Regional Hospital, where, in the presence of a doctor, he again refused to give a urine or blood sample.

Gomez was charged on Friday morning and granted bail to appear in the Orange Walk Magistrate’s Court on Monday, October 19. His car was impounded.

World.title: Excessive rainfall warning remains as Belize braces for another 2 to 4 inches of rain
World.content:
Excessive rainfall warning remains as Belize braces for another 2 to 4 inches of rain

The National Meteorological Service says an additional 2 to 4 inches of rain is likely over some areas in the next 12 to 24 hours. Residents are advised to monitor the weather and stay tuned to official updates.

A moist east northeasterly airflow continues over the country. Skies will be cloudy with sunny breaks today and cloudy at times tonight.

Showers and periods of light rain are affecting most areas this morning, but the activity is expected to decrease somewhat by the afternoon. Tonight, a few showers and some light rain will affect mainly the coast, with isolated thunderstorms possible.

Coastal areas will reach a high of 86°F (30°C) with a low of 79°F (26°C). Inland areas will hit 90°F (32°C), cooling to 73°F (23°C). The hills will see a high of 79°F (26°C) and a low of 68°F (20°C).

Today’s forecast was issued by forecaster Derrick Rudon.

World.content:
Public auction at Belmopan Aggregates and Hardware set for October 28
