NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde met Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff at his residence on Sunday night after a firing incident in Mumbai's Juhu area, assuring the actor and his family of the state government's support. Photographs from the meeting showed Shroff with bandages on his arm and dressings on his shoulder and chest.Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Shinde said five rounds had been fired during the incident, but the actor was safe. He added that Shroff had sustained injuries to his left hand due to gunpowder and glass shards, while his driver was injured in the incident."This is a major incident... five rounds were fired, but fortunately, he was safe. His driver sustained injuries, and the incident is condemnable. I met with the actor; he has injuries on his left hand caused by gunpowder and shards of glass. Both he and his mother are quite shaken... I have assured them that the state government stands with them in the face of the open threats being directed at public figures... No form of threat will be tolerated," Shinde said.Shinde visited the actor to enquire about his well-being after reports of gunshots being fired while Shroff was leaving a football club on Sunday evening.His mother, Ayesha Shroff, was also present during the meeting. Actor Disha Patani later arrived at Shroff's residence.Condemning the firing, Shinde said the state government would not tolerate attempts to intimidate public figures and assured the Shroff family that the authorities would take necessary steps to address the threat.Drawing a comparison with the gang-related violence witnessed in Mumbai in the 1990s, the deputy chief minister said the police had brought such activities under control and vowed to prevent their resurgence."Such gang wars were quite common in the 90s, but the Mumbai Police put an end to them in 1995... These attempts to intimidate people will not be tolerated, and we will put an end to this hooliganism," he said.Shinde's visit came amid concerns over the firing incident, with the state government assuring the actor and his family of its support. The police have maintained that Shroff was safe and had not suffered any gunshot wounds.

World.title: Omar Abdullah seeks action over attack on J&K-bound bus in Haryana

World.title: Espionage case on Army officer’s wife, lens on ‘China links’
World.content:

JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a case and started a probe against a Jammu-based Army officerâs wife for allegedly collecting and sharing sensitive information with foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, sources said Sunday.The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. She allegedly used AI tools ChatGPT and Claude to write papers on sensitive security issues for Chinese intelligence operatives suspected to have contacted her posing as academicians. The information was allegedly passed on through encrypted communication (online) mediums.The woman married the major-rank officer in 2023, a year after finishing a course in international governance from Geneva. She got a Masterâs degree from a Bengaluru university in 2021.A joint team of officers, including some from a central intelligence agency, intercepted the woman at Jammu railway station on Oct 14 when she was reportedly preparing to board a train to Pathankot. She was stopped and taken to a nearby military station for questioning, officials said. This followed a case filed at Jammuâs Gandhi Nagar Police Station under Official Secrets Act, and BNS sections relating to criminal conspiracy and offences against national sovereignty.A DSP assigned to lead the probe has questioned the woman, seizing her phone and extracting data that purportedly showed documents on sensitive subjects. The accused claimed her material was based entirely on open-source research supplemented by the AI platforms.The officials made it clear that despite being booked, the woman has not been arrested yet. Her interrogation indicated that she had interacted with several foreign nationals during her UN internship, including a Chinese national with whom she allegedly maintained contact through WhatsApp, the officials said. In 2024, she was in contact via social media with a Malaysian consultant allegedly working for Chinese intelligence agencies, the officials added.Preliminary investigations indicate the Chinese operatives initially made the woman write articles on environmental and geopolitics issues before gradually goading her to switch to defence matters. Investigators suspect she may have fallen into an âintellectual trapâ, not realising that those approaching her as academicians were actually operatives trying to extract sensitive information.Investigators are examining whether the woman engaged in systematic information-sharing under the guise of freelance research, adding a comprehensive forensic examination of her digital devices and financial transactions is on to establish the exact nature of the shared material, the officials said.(With inputs from agencies)

World.title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level â an altitude no other HC can ever match.

Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, âI am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.â

J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein.

Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many.

Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh.

âBut a name on a courtâs letterhead is not the same as a court on oneâs doorstepâ¦ The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,â he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani.





But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services.

âAccess to justice, after all, begins not in the courtâs compound, but at the litigantâs door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,â he said.

In an unprecedented gesture, the CJI said, âOnce video-conferencing facilities are adequately available to the lawyers of the Ladakh bench, Supreme Court shall list all matters coming from Ladakh on a single day, and hear them on a day-to-day basis, also through videoconferencing.â

âSomewhere in Ladakh today, in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra, there is a young child who will one day argue her first case in this court, and perhaps even sit on its bench as a judge. When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh but taken root here,â the CJI said.

World.title: 'Barged in, cut power': AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj claims Delhi Police harassing Bengali community in CR Park
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Saurabh Bharadwaj has accused Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park), alleging that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment.

He also warned that restrictions on Puja celebrations could lead to overcrowding, drawing a parallel with the Kolkata stampede that killed 17 people on Saturday.

In a post on X addressed to Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) state president claimed that the community and Puja organisers were facing unprecedented harassment.

âAttention @LtGovDelhi saab, Delhi Police officers are harassing the Bengali community and CR Park Durga Puja Committees like never before.

This community is one of the most decent and well-educated sections of Delhi,â he wrote.

Questioning the alleged disparity in the treatment of different cultural events, Bharadwaj referred to the Delhi government's position on allowing shops and businesses to operate round the clock and said most Ram Leela celebrations were permitted to continue past midnight.

âWhen the Delhi Govt talks about 24x7 businesses and shops, and most Ram-leelas are allowed past midnight, why the stepmotherly treatment for the Bengali community?â he asked.





Bharadwaj also alleged that police constables entered the B Block Durga Puja pandal on Saturday and cut its electricity connections. âYesterday, police constables barged into the B Block Durga Puja pandal and forcibly cut the electrical connections, damaging their equipment. This is not done,â he said.

In another post on X, Bharadwaj criticised the BJP over the reported West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy and raised concerns about crowd management at the Puja pandals.

âBJP has learnt nothing from the West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy,â he wrote.

He claimed that lakhs of people, including Bengalis and non-Bengalis, visit CR Park's Puja pandals every year, particularly in the evenings. He further alleged that Puja committees had been told that pandals and loudspeakers could operate only until 10 pm this year, compared with midnight last year.

This could lead to a West Bengal-type situation, and the government will prosecute puja committees to hide its own shortcomings,â Bharadwaj alleged.

Meanwhile, the Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II and adjoining areas of South Delhi from October 16 to 20, between 4 pm and midnight, citing the expected influx of visitors and limited road space around the pandals.

Private vehicles belonging to visitors and devotees will not be allowed to enter CR Park and Greater Kailash-II during the restricted hours. Commuters have been advised to use the Delhi Metro, with taxi and auto-rickshaw drop-off points designated at Greater Kailash and Nehru Enclave Metro stations. World.title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
World.content:
File photo: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam

JNU dismissal and police investigation

Akoijam says Manipur's wider crisis needs attention

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offered him a ticket, as he faces a sexual harassment case and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).Speaking at an event, the Inner Manipur MP said his decision to enter the electoral contest would be guided by the future of the state."I am ready to fight elections from Keishamthong (in Imphal West district). If the party offers me a ticket, I will contest the Keisamthong assembly constituency. This decision is for the future of the state," Akoijam said, according to news agency PTI.The Manipur Assembly elections are due next year.His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from JNU, where he was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.Akoijam was dismissed from the university on October 9 following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt", claiming he was not given an opportunity to respond to the inquiry committee's findings.Delhi Police booked him on October 11 following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. He recently appeared before investigators at the Vasant Kunj North Police Station in New Delhi in connection with the case.At least 11 female students submitted complaints against Akoijam in May. They alleged that he invited students to his campus residence on the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to harass them. Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks in class.After appearing before investigators, Akoijam said he intended to challenge his dismissal legally.Speaking to reporters in Imphal on Friday, he said his lawyers were preparing the case and that he would file it within a day or two.He also said he had cooperated with the police and would continue to do so, while requesting adequate notice for any further questioning because of his responsibilities as an MP.During his remarks to the media, Akoijam also urged greater attention to the wider situation in Manipur, including the plight of internally displaced people, lawlessness and issues surrounding buffer zones."Thousands of people are languishing in relief camps. I donât think my pain is anything greater than the pain of these people," he said, while alleging that the action against him was an attempt to silence his voice.The MP had earlier said, "Justice will be done," before travelling to New Delhi to join the police investigation.The allegations have also triggered political reactions in the state. BJP workers staged a protest outside Congress Bhavan in Imphal, demanding Akoijam's resignation and accusing him of bringing disrepute to Manipur. Police prevented the protesters from entering the premises.Congress spokesperson Hareshwar Goshwami described the protest as a diversionary tactic and accused the ruling party of deflecting attention from killings and the crisis in the state.Akoijam has maintained that the allegations against him are false and has challenged the process that led to his dismissal. The sexual harassment allegations remain under investigation.

World.title: Congress alleges ‘RSS employment scheme’ as Centre opens Census enumerator posts to private individuals
World.content:
A day after the Union government authorised the appointment of private schoolteachers and members of “institutions, societies and trusts” as Census enumerators, senior Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Saturday (October 17, 2026) alleged that the move appeared to be an employment scheme for Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) members.

A former Census official said that though the provision of “any person” being appointed as Census enumerators existed in the Census Rules, 1990, there was no precedent of private persons being engaged for the exercise, and a similar suggestion for the 1991 Census had not been accepted because of concerns over accountability, the official said.

The Population Enumeration (PE) phase, which will be conducted across the country in February 2027, also coincides with annual school examinations and board examinations. In poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa, the door-to-door enumeration will start on December 1 and end on January 4, 2027, followed by Assembly elections, where the government teachers will be put on election duty.

Most government school teachers have also been engaged as Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls over the past year.

Former Deputy Registrar General of India K. Narayanan Unni told The Hindu that the number of government schoolteachers had not increased in proportion to the population, which could mean a shortage of personnel for the Census.

“The move seems to have been triggered by the fact that not enough government schoolteachers, or even those from government-aided schools, are available for the exercise. Government schools have not grown in proportion to the population, and that is why the need to engage private teachers,” Mr. Unni said.

“No precedent of private people”

Though the category of “any person” existed in the Census Rules, 1990, the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India (RG&CCI) on Friday broadened the category of people who could be engaged as enumerators. Until now, mostly government schoolteachers, revenue officials and other State government employees had been engaged to carry out the enumeration work, and there was no precedent of private people being engaged in the previous Census.

During the first phase of Census 2027—the Houselisting Operations (HLO)—several private teachers in Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra and Haryana, who were asked by the State government to carry out the enumeration duty, moved courts and secured interim relief.

On Friday (October 16, 2026), the Punjab and Haryana High Court stayed two Haryana government communications seeking details of teachers for Census 2027, granting interim relief to private unaided schools against the deployment of their staff for the exercise.

Mr. Ramesh said in a post on X, “During July 10-12, 2026, the RSS held a big training camp in Belgaum for its cadres on the single-point agenda of Census 2027. The High-Level Committee on Demographic Changes set up by the Union Home Ministry on May 26, 2026, has just asked for inputs from the public, including Indian and foreign organisations, on demographic changes in the country. The only thing high level of this committee is the affiliation of its members to the RSS ecosystem. So we know where these inputs will come from.”

“The Census Notification of October 16, 2026 has to be seen in light of the RSS training camp of July 10-12, 2026 and the Demographic Change Committee’s call for inputs on October 14, 2026. It is clear this is a Rozgar Guarantee Yojana for thousands of RSS/BJP workers. This will most certainly further contaminate an already subverted Census. Another institution is being destroyed. Like SIR (Special Intensive Revision), the Census will also be dangerously doctored. There are no limits to the diabolical designs of the PM-HM duo,” he added.

Around 34 lakh enumerators are required for the PE phase, which will include 40 questions, several of which will be asked for the first time—spouse’s name, nationality, parents’ particulars, including their dates of birth and places of birth, digital literacy, permanent residential address and place of COVID-19 vaccination. Respondents will also be asked about the number of bank accounts they hold and whether they have a passport, driving licence and mobile phone, Aadhaar and voter ID.

Census 2027 will be India’s first digital Census and the first since Independence to enumerate castes other than Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

World.title: 36 new wildlife records put Keralam’s Peechi’s biodiversity in the spotlight
World.content:
From the Malabar Lark to the elusive Travancore Bambootail, Peechi’s forests have yielded a rich trove of biodiversity, with a four-day wildlife survey adding 36 species to existing checklists and recording 395 species of birds, butterflies and odonates across three sanctuaries.

Conducted from October 8 to 11 by the Forest and Wildlife department in association with the Travancore Nature History Society (TNHS), Thiruvananthapuram, the survey covered Chimmony Wildlife Sanctuary, Peechi–Vazhani Wildlife Sanctuary and Chulannur Peafowl Sanctuary through 10 base camps. It also recorded 24 species endemic to the Western Ghats, highlighting the conservation value of the landscape.

“The combination of checklist additions and Western Ghats endemics demonstrates the importance of systematic seasonal inventories and taxonomic verification,” said Kalesh Sadasivan, who coordinated the scientific compilation for TNHS.

Eight additions

Birdwatchers documented 165 species, including eight additions to the existing checklist. The notable records included the Malabar Lark (Galerida malabarica), Purple Heron (Ardea purpurea), Siberian Stonechat (Saxicola maurus) and Eastern Yellow Wagtail (Motacilla tschutschensis).

Five of the recorded birds are endemic to the Western Ghats: Malabar Grey Hornbill (Ocyceros griseus), Malabar Parakeet (Psittacula columboides), White-bellied Treepie (Dendrocitta leucogastra), Malabar Barbet (Psilopogon malabaricus) and Crimson-backed Sunbird (Leptocoma minima).

Butterflies accounted for the largest share of the records, with 174 species documented, including 22 additions to the earlier checklist. Among the notable additions were the Sahyadri Plain Puffin (Appias indra shiva), Common Map (Cyrestis thyodamas indica), Sahyadri Colour Sergeant (Athyma inara sahyadriensis), Bicolour Ace (Halpe hyrtacus) and Orange-spotted Ace (Thoressa honorei).

The survey recorded 11 Western Ghats-endemic butterflies, including the Malabar Banded Peacock (Papilio buddha), Malabar Rose (Pachliopta pandiyana), Sahyadri Lacewing (Cethosia mahratta), Southern Blue Oakleaf (Kallima horsfieldii), Travancore Evening Brown (Parantirrhoea marshalli) and Siva Sunbeam (Curetis siva).

The odonate survey documented 56 species, with six additions to the existing checklist. These included the Indian Emerald (Hemicordulia asiatica), Kodagu Clubtail (Gomphidia kodaguensis), Spotted Torrent-hawk (Epophthalmia frontalis binocellata), Coorg Bambootail (Caconeura ramburi), Malabar Bambootail (Melanoneura bilineata) and Blood-spotted Reedtail (Protosticta sanguinostigma).

Eight of the recorded odonates are endemic to the Western Ghats. Notable species included the Ruby-tailed Hawklet (Epithemis mariae), Fraser’s Torrent-dart (Euphaea fraseri), Travancore Bambootail (Esme mudiensis), Saffron Reedtail (Indosticta deccanensis) and Pied Reedtail (Protosticta gravelyi).

52 moth specie

Beyond the three principal groups, the survey recorded 52 moth species, 22 ant species, five cicada species and around 30 spider species. The presence of tigers, leopards, herds of Asian elephants and gaur further underscored the ecological significance of the forest landscape.

“Repeated surveys are essential to strengthen our knowledge of the wildlife of Peechi and Chimmony. The newly compiled records, particularly the endemic species, provide useful evidence for habitat management and future monitoring,” said M.K. Renjith, Wildlife Warden, Peechi Wildlife Division, who led the survey.

Conducted after the southwest monsoon, the October survey provides a seasonal baseline. A complementary pre-monsoon survey has been proposed to track seasonal changes in species composition, abundance, breeding activity and habitat use, particularly among butterflies, odonates and other invertebrates.

Comparing the two surveys could help distinguish resident species from seasonal visitors and improve the detection of species missed during individual assessments, strengthening long-term biodiversity monitoring and evidence-based management of the Peechi–Vazhani and Chimmony landscapes, the team said.

T.N. Rajesh, Assistant Wildlife Warden, Peechi; K.M. Muhammed Raphy, Assistant Wildlife Warden, Chimmony; and Salish Menachery, Wildlife Assistant, Peechi were part of the survey. TNHS’s technical coordination and scientific compilation were undertaken by Dr. Sadasivan and Anila V.M., research associate, with support from field experts, camp leaders and frontline forest staff.

World.title: Keralam Forest department removes fences, iron bars blocking movement of wild elephants in Chinnakkanal
World.content:
The Keralam Forest department has removed fences and iron bars blocking the movement of wild elephants in Chinnakkanal here following demands from local tribal residents.

The decision came out of talks held between forest officials, tribal residents, and people’s representatives at the Panthadikkalam tribal settlement under the Devikulam forest range, following the death of a tribal farmer. Vijayan, a resident of Panthadikkalam, was killed on the morning of September 23 in an attack by a wild elephant known locally as Chakkakompan.

Following the farmer’s death, local residents staged protests demanding the immediate removal of barricades obstructing elephant passages in Panthadikkalam. During the talks, revenue and forest officials conceded to the demand, and an agreement was signed by the Munnar Divisional Forest Officer (DFO). Based on this agreement, the Idukki District Collector issued an order to dismantle illegal fencing along the migration passages.

“Based on the agreement with the tribal community, department officials removed the fences obstructing elephant movement in Chinnakkanal. The barriers had trapped the animals in Panthadikkalam, leading to the tusker camping in the settlement and causing the tragic incident,” a forest official said.

Primary demand

C.V. Biju, a local tribal farmer, said fence removal had been their primary demand during the talks. “The day Vijayan was killed, I narrowly escaped an attack myself. Illegal fencing is the main hurdle blocking elephant passage. We met the District Collector in person and demanded its removal,” he said.

“Once the forest officials cleared the barriers, the elephant issue subsided. The wild tusker Chakkakompan moved toward Mathikettan Shola National Park. But now that landowners have reinstalled the fences, we are once again facing the threat of elephant attacks,” Mr. Biju added.

The Collector’s order and the subsequent demolition drew criticism from private property owners, leading several to reinstall the barriers.

Notices issued

Devikulam Forest Range Officer E.D. Arun Kumar said notices have been issued to 14 landowners who reinstalled fences within the range. “A meeting with the landowners has been scheduled for October 22 to address the matter,” the officer said, reiterating that the initial removal was carried out in response to firm demands from the tribal community.

Department sources confirmed that a report regarding the obstruction of elephant corridors in the Devikulam range has been submitted to the Devikulam Subcollector. The report urges the Revenue department to identify illegal encroachments on revenue land in Chinnakkanal and take decisive action to clear unauthorised fences across the area.

World.title: Govt. schemes should be delivered more effectively to farmers: Srinivas Poojary
World.content:
Udupi-Chikkamagaluru MP Kota Srinivas Poojary on Saturday said schemes of the Central and State governments for value addition to agricultural and horticultural produce should be delivered more effectively to the farming community to make farmers self-reliant.

He was speaking after inaugurating the Agriculture and Horticulture Fair at the Regional Agriculture and Horticulture Research Centre in Brahmavara, organised in collaboration with Keladi Shivappa Nayaka University of Agriculture and Horticultural Sciences (KSNUAHS), Shivamogga, and others.

The MP said, “We are witnessing many changes in agriculture in line with the current standard of living and technology. Today, more than 100 varieties of rice are being exhibited at the agricultural fair. This provides an opportunity for future generations in the farming community to build a livelihood.” He said significant changes were being witnessed in horticulture as well. Many people have improved their lives by cultivating multiple crops along with horticultural crops. There are examples before us of people sustaining themselves in society by relying on agriculture and horticulture for their livelihood.

Karnataka Coastal Development Board Chairman M.A. Gafur said, “Ours is an agricultural country. By implementing the Land Reforms Act, D. Devaraj Urs made about six lakh families in the coastal region landowners. Rice, sugarcane, arecanut and other crops are being grown in the coastal districts.”

He said Varahi water should be made available to farmers in the district, who have shown that a variety of crops can be grown even on small holdings. “Let us make a concerted effort to provide all kinds of support to farmers,” he said.

KSNUAHS Vice-Chancellor M.V. Dhananjaya, in his introductory address, said agriculture in coastal Karnataka is highly profitable. “We should continue to be climate-resilient, sustainable and technology-driven. Farmers should emerge as entrepreneurs by utilising opportunities for value addition,” he said.

The Agriculture Department released a technical handbook and the manuscript titled Chandada Maneyodatiyinda Andada Tarasi Tota (A beautiful terrace garden from a beautiful landlady). On the occasion, progressive farmers who won first place in the paddy crop competition under the Department of Agriculture’s ATMA Yojana between 2020-21 and 2024-25 were felicitated.

President of the Udupi District Farmers’ Society Ashok Kumar Kodgi, president of the Brahmavar Taluk Farmers’ Society P. Vaikuntha Herle, Joint Director of Agriculture G.C. Poornima, Joint Director of Horticulture Kshama Patil, Research Director of the Brahmavara Centre S. Sridhar, Extension Director Raghavendra K. Mesta, and others were present.
